entries.decision_rule: PRE-REGISTERED, before any arm has run. Three questions, answered per encoder. (a) ABSOLUTE GAP: for each of the nine arms, small-encoder recall@p75 minus the resnet101 row of backbone_benchmark.csv. Reported as a table with the encoder's own floor beside it; a gap inside the floor is UNDETERMINED, never "no difference". This number carries the warm-start confound stated in the hypothesis and is reported as encoder-plus-warm-start until a resnet101-from-ImageNet control exists. (b) SEED SPREAD: the encoder's own floor = max pairwise |delta| of recall@p75 among bbNN_2011s_base, _s2, _s3, compared with the resnet101 spread row of backbone_benchmark.csv (NOISE_FLOOR_2011s / spread / matched_p75). "Comparable" means within 2x; a floor above 2x the reference says the small encoder is too noisy to rank recipes at this sample size, regardless of (c). (c) RANK AGREEMENT — the licensing question: the positive pair (bbNN_2016_in05 minus bbNN_2016_base) must exceed the encoder's own floor from (b) with the SAME sign as resnet101, and the null pair (bbNN_2011s_cor05 minus bbNN_2011s_base) must fall inside it. If (c) holds for an encoder, recipe search is LICENSED on that encoder, with resnet101 reserved for confirmation runs and deliverables; if it fails, search stays on resnet101 and the failure mode (missed positive vs false positive) is recorded. Two encoders can license independently; the cheaper one that passes wins. SECOND QUEUE SHAPE: the primary metric needs the Phase-B2 inference over the sample blocks (--infer-aoi science_sample_blocks.gpkg WITHOUT --sample-manifest, the Tier-1 commit ac0e79e shape), then qc/phase4_qc_indep.py scoring on the LOSO test blocks and a harvest_arm_metrics re-run. Per-step flags are impossible in one queue job, so that is a follow-up queue generated from this file with steps [inference]; (a)-(c) are not readable before it runs. CANARY: each launch file runs a distinct-tag, 1+1-epoch copy of the 2006s base arm FIRST (canary_bb18_2006s_base / canary_bb50_2006s_base) so one full labels->tile->train->evaluate cycle lands under --encoder before the nine arms spend; the canary's numbers are plumbing evidence only and are never scored. GPU: the 2-concurrent-A100 cap; one queue file per A100. PHASE 2 (added 2026-09-09, before any wb50 arm ran): the warm-started wb50_ arms are the read that counts for (a), (b) and (c) — they start from the encoder_bases base50 checkpoint, so (a) is an encoder comparison without the warm-start confound stated in the hypothesis. The bb50_ rows remain the ImageNet-start record. Phase-2 launch files carry NO canary: --encoder and the labels->tile->train->evaluate cycle were proven by phase 1, and the --ckpt load path is the engine's ordinary p3_ckpt route.

extra.kam_decision_2026_09_09: KAM, 2026-09-09, on extra.phase2_result_pending_kam: "move forward with using resnet 18 to refine the recipe." READ AS OPTION (i): resnet50 from the base50 start is accepted on (a) the absolute gap, (b) the seed spread and the null pair, and recipe refinement now moves DOWN to resnet18 — PROVIDED the resnet18 phase-2 check holds the way resnet50's did: (a) at or above the resnet101 record at the held cut (matched_p75 recall, phase4/qc/backbone_benchmark.csv), (b) its own three-seed spread comparable to the 101's 0.0085 (the pre-registered "within 2x"), and the null pair (wb18_2011s_cor05 minus wb18_2011s_base) inside that floor. If any of the three fails, recipe search does NOT move to resnet18 and the failure is recorded here. WHAT THIS GATE DROPS, stated plainly: the pre-registered (c) also required the POSITIVE pair (2016 in05 minus base) to clear the encoder's floor with the 101's sign. resnet50 did not meet it and this decision does not require resnet18 to. The reason is the reference arm, not the small encoder — the 101's t1_2016_base (0.669) was recorded suspect-low on 2026-09-03 while every warm-started encoder lands at the ~0.751 ceiling. THE 2016 LIDAR EFFECT THEREFORE STAYS **UNRESOLVED**, not disproven: it cannot be read until the 101's 2016 base is reseeded, which is already on the board. No verdict is written for this experiment on the strength of the positive pair either way. The older extra.phase2_warm_started sentence ("ResNet-18 phase 2 runs ONLY if resnet50 passes rank agreement (c)") is the pre-decision record; this note supersedes it.

extra.phase2_result_pending_kam: PHASE 2 SCORED 2026-09-09 (the pre-registered metric: matched_p75 recall at held ~0.75 precision vs C-CAP 2021 on the LOSO sample-test blocks; phase4/qc/arm_metrics.csv, eval_scope sample-test, joined to backbone_benchmark.csv). Warm-started resnet50 vs the resnet101 record, recall (precision): 2011s base 0.762 (0.752) vs 0.725 (0.750); s2 0.751 vs 0.720; s3 0.753 vs 0.717; cor05 0.752 vs 0.725; 2016 base 0.751 vs 0.669 (0.758); 2016 in05 0.758 vs 0.744; 2020 base 0.678 (0.771) vs 0.640 (0.800). AP within +/-0.006 on 2011s/2016, +0.02 on 2020. (a) ABSOLUTE GAP: none - resnet50 from the base50 start is ABOVE the 101 on every arm (+0.014 to +0.082 recall at the held cut). (b) NOISE: seed spread 0.0114 vs the 101's 0.0085 - comparable (1.3x). (c) RANK AGREEMENT, as pre-registered: NOT MET on the positive pair. The 101 read 2016 in05 - base = +0.075 (9x its floor); resnet50 reads +0.0066 (0.6x its floor), i.e. no effect. The null pair agrees (-0.010 vs -0.0002, both inside the floor). THE DISAGREEMENT SITS IN THE 101'S BASELINE, not in the small encoder: t1_2016_base (0.669) was already recorded as suspect-low in the 2026-09-03 plan ("all five 2016 treatments cluster at the same ceiling"), and resnet50's 2016 base lands at that ceiling (0.751), so the lidar-input "gain" on the 101 is consistent with a low baseline rather than a treatment effect. The rule as written does not license recipe search on resnet50; the evidence says the rule's own reference arm is the doubtful one. NEEDS KAM: (i) accept resnet50 (base50 start) for recipe search on (a)(b) and the null pair, treating the 2016 lidar effect as UNRESOLVED until the 101's 2016 base is reseeded (already on the board), or (ii) hold the rule literally and reseed first. ResNet-18 phase 2 stays gated on that decision. Cache fix validated on the in05 re-run (one stage line, cache hits, no ENOENT).

entries.hypothesis: Recipe rankings measured on a small encoder agree with resnet101 within the noise floor, so recipe search (the dozens of label/input/loss knobs still open after Tier-1) can move to the small encoder and resnet101 is reserved for confirmation and deliverables. The nine Tier-1 arms in phase4/qc/backbone_benchmark.csv are the reference: five base years, the 2011s three-seed floor, one CONFIRMED-POSITIVE pair (2016 in05 vs 2016 base, lidar input, the largest of the 3/3 confirmed deltas in tier1_results.csv) and one NULL pair (2011s cor05 vs 2011s base, the flat corruption dose inside the floor). Each is re-run on resnet18 and resnet50 with everything else held: same tiles recipe (--force-citywide --sample-manifest, no hillshade except the in05 arm's chm2005 band 4), same decoder (config.DECODER_CHANNELS), same epoch budgets, same seeds. What would change our mind: the positive pair failing to read positive, or the null pair reading positive, against the encoder's OWN three-seed floor — then the small encoder cannot be trusted to rank recipes and search stays on 101. STATED CONFOUND (config.py, ENCODER AS A RUN FLAG block): every resnet101 arm warm-started from the Phase-3 2020 base — a 2020-trained encoder AND decoder — while a resnet18/50 arm has no such base and starts from ImageNet encoder weights with a random decoder (warm_start stamp: p3_ckpt vs imagenet). Question (a) below therefore measures encoder PLUS warm start; (b) and (c) are within-encoder reads and do not carry that confound. A resnet101-from-ImageNet control arm would separate the two and is recommended before (a) is read as an encoder effect.
entries.metric: PRIMARY: LOSO sample-test recall at held precision 0.75 (policy matched_p75) per arm, from phase4/qc/arm_metrics.csv rows with ref ccap_2021_hires_lc.tif, canopy_def forest_wetland, eval_scope sample-test — the identical basis as the resnet101 rows in phase4/qc/backbone_benchmark.csv. Deltas are read arm minus its resnet101 twin, and pair deltas within an encoder (in05 minus base; cor05 minus base). COST: wall-clock minutes per step from the per-launch train_queue_status_*.csv ledger (column minutes) and the step logs under phase4/logs/; peak GPU memory from the raw hw_{session}.csv telemetry (gpu_mem_used_mb, sliced by the run_tag column of the v2 schema) — no per-arm peak column exists yet and one must be harvested, not typed. SECONDARY: best_f1 rows of the same population; the circular semantic_eval_report.csv row is recorded (it now carries encoder + warm_start) but is never the headline.

entries.sample: The Tier-1 ground sample: 33 screened blocks split once (30 test, 2 train, 1 selection; phase4/qc/science_sample_manifest.csv), the same fixed blocks for every arm and every encoder. Train and early-stop on the manifest tiles; scores read from the test blocks only. Every arm re-tiles under its own tag (tile_dir_for keys on {label}__{run_tag}); the offload pilot measured a re-tile as byte-identical, so the tiles are the same set under a new name, at the cost recorded in extra.measured_cost.
entries.verdict: DECIDED 2026-09-10 on Kam's gate (extra.kam_decision_2026_09_09): RECIPE REFINEMENT MOVES TO RESNET-18, warm-started from phase4/models/sem_best_2020_base18.pt. The pre-registered metric (matched_p75 recall vs C-CAP 2021 on the LOSO sample-test blocks; phase4/qc/arm_metrics.csv joined to backbone_benchmark.csv), resnet18 (base18 start) vs the resnet101 record: 2011s base/s2/s3 0.720/0.725/0.727 vs 0.725/0.720/ 0.717 (SEED SPREAD 0.0069 vs 0.0085); cor05 0.727 vs 0.725; 2016 base 0.743 vs 0.669; 2016 in05 0.751 vs 0.744; 2020 base 0.740 (P 0.753) vs 0.640 (P 0.800). AP 0.803-0.830 vs 0.755-0.820. (a) at or above the 101 on every arm; (b) noise better than the 101's; null pair +0.006, inside the floor. Positive pair +0.008 (inside the floor) — as on resnet50, the 101's +0.075 lidar-input effect does not reproduce with a sound baseline; the 2016 lidar effect stays UNRESOLVED pending the 101's 2016 reseed. Against resnet50 (base50 start): resnet18 is ~0.03 lower on 2011s, equal on 2016, higher on 2020; train 14-31 min vs 14-30 (both ~25-35% under the 101; the pipeline is I/O-bound, so the small encoder's saving is in fine-tune minutes, not inference). Phase-1 (ImageNet-start) arms stand as the record of why a trained base per encoder is required. Cache fix (0080cce) validated live twice (in05 inference on both encoders).

entries.decision_rule: PRE-REGISTERED. The two arms are NOT compared to each other and neither is promoted: each becomes the warm start for its encoder in a re-run of backbone_sweep. HOW: the checkpoint lands at phase4/models/sem_best_2020_{tag}.pt (core.step_evaluate: MODELS_DIR / f"sem_best_{label}{_tag_sfx()}.pt"), so a sweep arm passes --ckpt /content/drive/MyDrive/treedata/phase4/models/sem_best_2020_base50.pt (or _base18.pt) with the matching --encoder; ckpt.resolve_p3_ckpt refuses a missing path, ckpt._assert_state_fits refuses a key mismatch, and load_state_into inflates the first conv for a 4-band arm as it does for the P3 base. NOTE the stamp: ckpt.warm_start_kind(override) returns "p3_ckpt" for ANY explicit --ckpt, so those sweep rows will read warm_start=p3_ckpt with a base50/base18 start — distinguishable only through the manifest argv (run_passport.csv), and they need NEW tags (every tag is owned by one entry). GATE per arm: VERIFY:train OK with the checkpoint stamped encoder=resnet50|resnet18; an evaluate log with the four metrics over 150 tiles; a base whose test IoU sits far below the Phase-3 report on the same tiles (read from the lake file named in baseline) is NOT used as a start and the failure is recorded here. CONFOUND REMOVED by these arms: the 2020-trained start is now available for all three encoders. CONFOUND REMAINING: extra.remaining_confound.

extra.hazard: NEVER run --step tile or --force-retile under tags base50 / base18: the materialized meta cannot equal a live tiling._tile_signature, so step_tile would re-tile the citywide recipe over the crown tiles. Both queue files stop at [train, evaluate].
extra.measured_cost: Comparators from the tracked ledger, A100-40GB: t1_2020_base (resnet101, 343 train / 134 val tiles, blocked split) train 37.3 min + evaluate 4.2 min (phase4/qc/train_queue_status_*.csv, job tier1_science_sample_t1_2020_base); heal_2020 (438 train) train 39.2 min (run_registry.csv step_minutes). The lake's per-launch backbone ledger (untracked, read 2026-09-09) has bb18_2020_base (resnet18, same 343/134 set) train 41.2 min — resnet18 was NOT faster at this size, so no small-encoder discount is assumed. These arms train on ~478 of 598 (fold 0 of the 5-fold buffer split, buffer 512 px at stride 512 retains every neighbour) with ~120 val — ~1.4x the tile count — plus tile staging (timing_events `stage tiles 2020` 478.6 s for t1_2020_base) and ~150-tile evaluate: EXPECTED 50-60 min train + ~8 min staging + 3-5 min evaluate, ~60-75 min per queue, two queues on two A100s (the cap). An estimate, not a measurement.
extra.recipe_deltas: Matched: EPOCHS_PHASE_A 20 / EPOCHS_PHASE_B 30, LR 5e-5 / 5e-6, BATCH_SIZE 10, EARLY_STOP_PAT 15, ReduceLROnPlateau(factor 0.5, patience 5), SAVE_EVERY 5, ImageNet encoder weights (config.py vs phase3_semantic_dev.py, grepped 2026-09-09). Differ: the phase4 engine pins the frozen encoder's BatchNorm (FREEZE_ENCODER_BN True, no Phase-3 equivalent), selects with SELECT_SMOOTH_K 1 (no smoothing), draws its val fold by splits._choose_val_split, and applies its own loss/aug stack (losses.py, IGNORE-aware); Phase-3's WARMUP_EPOCHS 3 is only wired in its discriminative-unfreeze mode, not the baseline. Deltas beyond these constants were NOT audited.
extra.remaining_confound: The Phase-3 resnet101 base was initialised from the Phase-0 DDT instance- segmentation checkpoint (phase3_semantic_dev.py: ddt_best_v7_global.pt, encoder + decoder) BEFORE its Phase A/B, and that checkpoint exists only for resnet101 — it is not reproducible for resnet18/50, so these bases start from ImageNet encoder weights + a random decoder (ckpt.load_imagenet_encoder). Also the Phase-3 base was trained by the Phase-3 script, these by the phase4 engine (recipe_deltas).

entries.headline: BOTH BASES LANDED 2026-09-09 (one A100 each; no runtime remains).
entries.hypothesis: A 2020-trained base for EACH encoder — resnet50 and resnet18, trained on the SAME tiles the Phase-3 resnet101 base (phase3/sem_best_2020.pt) was trained on — removes the warm-start confound stated in experiments/backbone_sweep.yaml: today every resnet101 arm starts from a 2020-trained encoder AND decoder while a resnet18/50 arm starts from ImageNet encoder weights and a random decoder (config.py, ENCODER AS A RUN FLAG block; warm_start stamp p3_ckpt vs imagenet). With a same-trained start per encoder, a re-run of the sweep reads as an ENCODER comparison. The tiles are the Phase-3 crown tiles, materialized under phase4 tags by qc/instruments/phase3_tiles_as_tileset.py from phase3/tiles/tile_index_semantic.csv — the INDEX rows, which are what Phase-3 train/evaluate read, not the directory (counts: phase4/qc/tileset_registry.csv row 2020__base50; the tiles on disk that no index row names are counted in the directory's meta sidecar, split_status.orphan_tiles_not_indexed). What would change our mind: a base whose held-out test score on the Phase-3 test tiles is far below the Phase-3 resnet101 report on the same tiles (baseline, on the lake) is a base that did not train, and must not be used as a start. STATED HONESTLY: this is the Phase-3 TILES under the phase4 engine's fine-tier recipe, not a re-run of the Phase-3 script — see extra.recipe_deltas — and the one confound that REMAINS is extra.remaining_confound.
entries.metric: PRIMARY: held-out test IoU / Dice / Prec / Rec on the 150 Phase-3 test tiles from each arm's evaluate step log, phase4/logs/phase4_semantic_finetune_evaluate_2020_ <ts>.log (the durable home; phase4/eval/semantic_eval_report.csv is shared across runtimes and was clobbered 2026-09-09 — backbone_sweep.yaml extra.cross_vm_eval_report_clobber — so a VERIFY:evaluate MISSING row is that defect until shown otherwise). The row is harvested to phase4/qc/eval_from_logs.csv by qc/instruments/eval_rows_from_logs.py. This split is sitewise_random_test at stride 512: non-overlapping tiles, NOT spatially blocked, NOT LOSO — read it as a training sanity number, never as an honest hold-out; the honest Phase-3 number is the LOSO report. COST: train and evaluate minutes from the per-launch train_queue_status_*.csv ledger (column minutes) and the step logs.

entries.verdict:
RAN 2026-09-08 02:02Z to 03:49Z (spdvc1 CPU labels+tile, spdvg A100 train), scored by an independent referee against the rule above; every number below names its file. K1 PASS - tileset_registry.csv row 2017k/spdv_2017k = a36d6772e88b, 632 tiles (third directory on that id). K2 PASS - no refusal or fallback string in the train log; the bundle path ran all thirteen checks and staged 1264 files from one read. R1 FAIL - timing_events.csv: "stage tiles 2017k" 123.7 s ("bundle copy" 119.2 s) against the 60 s bar and the 13-17 s prediction; 1.85x faster than the pilot's 228.2 s, which the rule does not credit. The flag is NOT promoted. Mechanism from hw_spdvg.csv: net rx moved ~0.41 GB in the first ~15 s, then >= 86 s with zero bytes on every channel, CPU 0.4-4.5%, iowait pinned at 8.4% (one of twelve vCPUs blocked) - a stall, not a slow copy. The comparator was wrong at this size class: stage rows for 0.10-0.33 GB objects (the band that reproduces on the tracked CSV; the referee wrote 0.01, whose p10 is 2.6) (n=82) run p10 7.5 / median 48.0 / max 959 MB/s, 16 of 82 under 10 MB/s. Transport (shutil.copyfile over the mount) ruled out - the same call moved 11.5 GB at 40.3 MB/s one step earlier; sha256 read-back and contention ruled out by the timer scope and the trace; a Drive latency window is SUPPORTED - spdvc1's rclone upload of the identical 1264 files took 1302 s against the pilot's 522 s on a byte-identical command line - and object freshness is NOT ruled out (n=1 comparable read). Design gap named: the read is a bare copyfile with no timeout, throughput floor or slow-path escape; its worst case is unbounded where the rclone path it replaces is not. R2 PASS - "startup:" lines: 79 status files in 5.1 s (spdvg) and 5.9 s (spdvc1), 78 bulk-copied, against the 60 s bar and the 359 s the ledger docstrings record for spdc1 (the pilot had no startup line). spdvg's beacon scan read 47.1 s with one open; the timer cannot separate the listing from the open, so that cost is UNDETERMINED. R3 PASS - zero "* installing" lines across both sessions' five logs (pilot: three). R4 PASS - hw_spdvc1.csv 792 rows, sampled/span 100.08%, 0 gaps, 0 torn; hw_spdvg.csv 468 rows, 99.28%, 0 gaps, 0 torn; the pilot's three files ran 76-85% with 1-4 torn rows. R5 PASS - hw_step_attribution.csv carries launching/open/verifying for both sessions; all five VERIFY rows in the two per-launch status files carry minutes (0.0-0.1).
DECISION - PHASE4SEG_TILE_BUNDLE stays OFF by default (R1 failed its bar). The four other changes validated on their own reads and stand: queue start-up bulk fetch (94cb8df), bootstrap requirements install (3f60b0f), hw logger spool+mirror (e8dec13), queue-side phases and VERIFY minutes (c5dc91c).
ALSO MEASURED, not decided. (i) Tile regressed +864 s engine time vs the pilot's CPU slice; ~780 s of it is the rclone upload of the same files (1302 vs 522 s), the bundle cost 31 s; host CPU is UNDETERMINED (no cpu_model on either meta; now recorded for future sessions, 8bd256c). Launching phases measured exactly: labels 9.25 min, tile 12.75 min at 36-50% iowait on 2 vCPU - the site-footprint discovery that 6276207 removed/moved AFTER this runtime cloned. (ii) Train 35.9 min engine vs 39.9 pilot: -104.5 s is the staging line (the only part the rule credits to the bundle); -148 s is one fewer checkpoint save and per-save variance over the same 50 epochs. Saving epochs average 58.0 s vs 24.4 s non-saving: 674 s over 20 saves, of which the timed copy is 49.6 s - the remaining 11-13 min per train step (torch.save, sha256 read-back through the mount, publish, Drive verify) is UNTIMED and the A100 idles through it. (iii) The one 35.9 s sem_best copy was the mount's write blocking with net tx at zero; its Drive verification succeeded BECAUSE the copy was slow, not the reverse.
NEXT, in order - (1) re-stage the now-aged a36d6772e88b bundle on a fresh A100 with the trace running (~1 min GPU): >= 30 MB/s says window/freshness, ~4 MB/s with the same zero-traffic stall says structural; (2) if structural, a chunked copy with a per-chunk tick, a throughput floor and a slow-path escape to the rclone transport; (3) regardless of the bundle, ticks around torch.save, _sha256(part) and verify_on_drive - four times the bundle's whole saving sits there, untimed.

entries.verdict: NO FIELD SUPPLIES A MEASURED LAUNDERING RATE for a one-directional temporal correction on real gold. Four fields (occupancy modelling, HMM/state-space, interval-censored survival, astronomy completeness) converge on one fill-odds formula whose denominator is P(regain | recent removal); the endpoint panel cannot measure it (its two gains are colonisation of empty sites), so the posterior cannot refuse a bracketed fill at the project's rates. Ranking: occupancy 7, HMM 7, interval-censored 6, label-noise/PU 6, multi-object tracking 5, image primitives 5, astronomy 4, speech/VAD 4, video segmentation 4, medical longitudinal 3. What stands: morphological closing as the comparator baseline, the gap-length spectrum H(L) as an instrument, the OVER-style attributed-error audit, PU's e(x) as a weight, F-space debiasing as an audit. FIRST THREE: (1) a fill-side laundering audit of ~300 cells sampled from the healer's own output, paired interval reads with a null-change control, reported beside the 0/42; (2) H(L) with laundered(L), triples(L), n_eligible and crowns-deleted columns, zero labels, mutation-tested; (3) measure gamma_conditional from adjudicated impossible triples at the no-change points (the 42 losses are selected for no regain and cannot yield it). REFUSE until gamma_conditional is measured: any posterior-as-licence (PMBM existence, dynamic-occupancy posterior, SAR-EM, fitted-transition HMMs).

R3 FAIL - postproc 26.9 min (log) / 27.1 (queue) against the 18.0 bar. The staging path DID engage (the log reads stage edmonds_canopy_prob_2017k_spd_2017k.tif 114.1s for 2.4 GB, and the windowed read ran off NVMe), so this is not the fallback; it is compute on a 2-vCPU / 13.3 GB runtime - polygonize 653.1 s vs 436.1 on the A100 box. Postproc offload is therefore NOT promoted as a queue default; it converts about 1.6 CU (inferred) into about 9 extra minutes on the critical path unless pipelined. Whether the staged read beats the FUSE read on the SAME machine is UNDETERMINED here - the machine changed too. A larger CPU tier is untested. R4 (direction only; marker basis for the pilot) - train GPU-busy 0.1961 vs 0.1792 on the interval-basis baseline, inference 0.7426 vs 0.7586; the marker basis confirms the interval basis on this arm, with the caveat that the A100 session's logger lost 26% of its samples to its own Drive flush (fix in progress). R5 sanity - AP 0.4338 vs 0.4275, AUROC 0.8860 vs 0.8851; the retrained model is the same model. Total wall-clock 154.9 min vs 113, as pre-stated (three bootstraps, sequential launches, 5-9 min queue start-up gaps that 94cb8df targets).
DECISION - labels+tile move to free CPU runtimes as the default (K2 proves equivalence, R1 measures the saving); train, evaluate, inference and postproc stay on the GPU box until a CPU tier with more than two cores is measured. Both code changes are validated on real data - P1 by R2 and the train delta, P2 by the staging line and the NVMe read.

entries.headline: THE STEP-SHAPE CERTIFIER WINS AND THE SHIPPED PERSISTENCE FILTER IS A PURE RECALL TAX.
entries.hypothesis: The shipped hot-spot rule filters map loss by requiring the loss to persist into a later epoch. Two questions were open and both were Kam's: can a year's neighbours vouch for it (borrow shape across the 8-epoch stack), and is persistence the right filter at all. The suspicion driving the campaign is that the two are opposite instruments — a real removal is a STEP, flat before and flat after, while neighbour consensus measures CURVATURE, so the more genuinely sustained a loss is, the less any smoothing or consensus rule can see it. What would change our mind: a consensus statistic that fires on sustained events at a rate comparable to a level-step statistic, or a persistence filter that buys precision worth its recall cost.

entries.verdict: THE STEP-SHAPE CERTIFIER WINS AND THE SHIPPED PERSISTENCE FILTER IS A PURE RECALL TAX. Bolting a fit-free step-shape certifier onto the existing two-epoch rule moves Olofsson-weighted precision from 0.249 to 0.431 — about 60 percent of the total gain any candidate achieved, for roughly five lines on the already-cached 2 m stack, no model and no fitted parameter — read from Reports/CHANGE_DETECTOR_DESIGN_2026-09-06.md, whose table also carries the recall column and the two model tiers. Once the certifier is attached the HMM-versus-slope question is statistically empty. The incumbent measured WORSE than believed: the persistence filter moves weighted precision by a statistical zero while deleting every one of the human-verified terminal-epoch losses by construction, because no later epoch exists to corroborate them. Mechanism, and the answer to Kam's question: neighbours may WEIGHT a year's testimony and must never overwrite it — a median-style correction regresses the best-calibrated year toward its worst-calibrated neighbours, endpoints cannot be smoothed so the bias never cancels, and the trap is spatial as well as temporal (a single removed crown inside a surviving stand is voted back by its own neighbours). Scope is fixed by the same read: Panel A stays the pace authority and this detector owns WHERE only, hard-limited to 2016-2024, because run backward the model fabricates a trend at the unvalidated endpoints. TWO STANDING CAVEATS: the prototype numbers were produced in session scratch and are, in the report's own words, unreproducible from repo plus lake until the certifier port lands — so this verdict is a design read, not a measured instrument; and the build itself (gold-set freeze, certifier port with its three audit fixes, tiered output) is QUEUED on Kam's go.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the flicker instrument's own gate, which predates this campaign by weeks and is stated in its docstring before any number: false positives that are STATIC cancel in year-to-year differencing and can be tolerated, while false positives that FLICKER manufacture spurious gain and loss and are the worst error mode a change product can have. entries.headline: THE MODEL DOES NOT HALLUCINATE CANOPY ON BARE GROUND; THE INSTABILITY LIVES IN SENSITIVITY ON REAL VEGETATION.
entries.hypothesis: The 8-year map series sawtooths by several pp a year around a signal of about two, and the whole trend read depends on WHERE that instability lives. Two candidate homes, and they demand opposite remedies: the model hallucinates canopy on non-vegetated ground (a false-positive problem, fixable with a height or greenness prior), or its sensitivity on REAL vegetation drifts by delivery (a calibration problem, fixable only at the operating point). Items 1 and 6 of the flicker program split the question: score every year on ground known not to have changed, then census every pixel's 8-year label trajectory citywide. What would change our mind about the first: false canopy on hard-negative parcels that moves across years rather than sitting flat.

entries.verdict: THE MODEL DOES NOT HALLUCINATE CANOPY ON BARE GROUND; THE INSTABILITY LIVES IN SENSITIVITY ON REAL VEGETATION. The three genuinely non-vegetated footprints (Parking, Water, Civic_Field) hold 0.0 to 0.7 percent false canopy, flat across all eight years, read from phase4/qc/trend8_flicker_report.csv — well inside the instrument's static gate, so the sawtooth is not a false-positive problem and no height or greenness prior would touch it. The same file also retired two of its own parcels: the Cemetery and Stadium footprints carry real crowns and track the city series, which makes them unusable as clean negatives — a correction to the negative set, not a result about the model. The census half is the counterweight and points the other way: on the citywide 2 m stack, per-pixel label trajectories are unstable at a scale no reference-scored accuracy number reveals, and a substantial share of the city carries the canopy-gone-canopy triple that no physical process can produce — both shares in phase4/qc/trend8_transition_census.csv, which is assumption-free because no reference raster and no threshold choice enters it. Put together the two halves isolate the error: it is per-year detection sensitivity on vegetated ground, so change MAPS need persistence or shape filtering even where change TOTALS at matched cuts corroborate direction. Both files are consumed downstream — the hard negatives become the empirical null and the zero-fire gate for change_detector_design, and the cached 2 m stack this campaign built is the I/O amortizer every later trajectory pass reuses.

entries.headline: NO TWIN EXISTS, AND THE ONE DESIGN THAT PASSED THE CHECKLIST WAS REFUSED ON ITS OWN PILOT.
entries.hypothesis: The project's central claim to novelty was ASSERTED, not hunted: that nobody has mapped canopy wall-to-wall from a heterogeneous, uncalibrated, sub-meter aerial archive over five or more epochs, measured the map series' own inter-date inconsistency, and validated the change against blind human truth. Either a twin study exists — in which case we adopt its method and stop reinventing — or a solution we have not considered exists, or neither does and the gap claim is upgraded from asserted to hunted. What would change our mind: any single study scoring 4 of 5 on the pre-written criteria, or a design surviving the adversarial checklist AND certifying on our data.

entries.sample: the unit is the PAPER. Nine contract angles, each with multiple query formulations across web search, Google Scholar phrase queries, Internet Archive Scholar full text, preprint servers, citation graphs and non-English grey literature; candidates triaged from the logged queries, finalists read in full and scored by independent adjudication panels against the contract's five criteria. entries.verdict: NO TWIN EXISTS, AND THE ONE DESIGN THAT PASSED THE CHECKLIST WAS REFUSED ON ITS OWN PILOT. Condition A is met on the letter by exactly one study — Roman et al. 2021, Land 10(4):403, Philadelphia 1970-2010, five epochs from two uncalibrated aerial programs, one interpreter, paired points with an interpreter-derived detectable-change threshold — adjudicated 4 of 5 by three independent panels and missing only segmentation. It is therefore the peer-reviewed precedent for Panel A's exact method, never for a map series; Nix and Healy extend it into a three-study lineage. No segmentation-series twin surfaced in 1,359 logged queries with 132 full-text reads and 42 recorded UNREADABLE, so the paper's gap claim is now hunted rather than asserted. Condition B is the more consequential half: PACC — panel is the estimator, map is the auxiliary — passed the adversarial checklist unanimously on the kill-test item, then its own read-only pilot showed the map series shrinks the panel's confidence interval by only about 4 percent (+-1.89 to +-1.81 pp) and that forcing the map to carry the difference is WORSE than ignoring it (+-3.68 pp), read from Reports/LIT_HUNT_FINAL_2026-09-06.md. B was refused despite the checklist pass, because the pilot failed the contract's purpose — which the digest's two-reader audit records as under-claiming rather than overclaiming. That refusal converged independently with the same day's change_detector_design conclusion: the map owns WHERE, Panel A owns PACE.

entries.headline: THE KNOBS THAT SOUND DEFINITIONAL ARE WORTH ~NOTHING; THE INVISIBLE ONES CARRY THE WHOLE ANSWER.
entries.hypothesis: The study's core variable had never been written down, and every instrument in the pipeline was quietly running its own version of it. Kam's four plain questions — is canopy what you see looking straight down at high noon; do small breaks inside a crown count; is there a gap-size threshold; does density matter — each name a knob the code already sets implicitly. The campaign's premise is that a definition is only worth arguing about in proportion to what it MOVES on our own data. What would change our mind: a sensitivity table in which the gap and morphology knobs — the ones that sound definitional — move city area more than the operating point, the reference family, or the denominator.

entries.verdict: THE KNOBS THAT SOUND DEFINITIONAL ARE WORTH ~NOTHING; THE INVISIBLE ONES CARRY THE WHOLE ANSWER. The literal gap knobs — 3x3 morphology plus the 3 m2 sieve — measured area-neutral at 1264.0 vs 1263.8 ha, read from phase4/qc/postproc_variant_scores.csv (morph vs morph_sieve, 2011s), while the reference family, the model operating threshold, the denominator and the interpreter's own consistency each move the headline by more, every one of them cited to its own measured file in the review's section-5 table. Mechanism: within-crown gaps are already closed by the classifier's receptive field long before postproc sees them, so the morphological "gap rule" operates on pixels that were never in dispute; the disputed pixels live at the greenness/height cut, the threshold, and the choice of ground in the denominator. Section 1 also settles the plain questions against the literature: vertical projection is the standard and matches Kam's high-noon intuition, crowns are treated as solid outlines (crown cover), and isolated trees count identically to stands. TWO STANDING CAVEATS the entry carries with the verdict: the written definition in section 6 is a DRAFT — section 7 hands six decisions back to Kam and the K4 sign-off row on the WORKPLAN board is open, so nothing here is adopted; and the review flags its own evidence base as partly contaminated, because every height-knob row measured on the old lidar_snoh_chm scale is UNDETERMINED pending a chm2 rebuild, including the "trees, not shrubs" reading of the contested band.

The design commitments: strata cross REFERENCE AGREEMENT with CANOPY HEIGHT, not model confidence, because uniform strata would spend the sample on ground both references already agree about; every stratum keeps its true area W_h = N_h/N, which is what makes the deliberate over-sampling of the contested zone unbiased rather than merely convenient; the four confusion cells within a stratum are ONE multinomial draw, so the CI carries the full covariance and not the sum of variances; `unsure` is a first-class answer, EXCLUDED from estimation and never coerced, the same three-state discipline as the mask labels (CLAUDE.md 3.6). The publication rule the campaign exists to enforce: mask-derived areas are labelled MAP AREA, and nothing is published as an area ESTIMATE until it carries the adjusted estimator and its CI (docs/STATS_CHECKLIST.md section 8). The design is admissible only if the measured power says it can tell the two candidate canopy definitions apart at the drawn n.

entries.headline: THE DESIGN HOLDS, THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS THE INTERPRETER RATHER THAN n, AND NO ESTIMATE HAS EVER BEEN PRODUCED.
entries.hypothesis: Every accuracy number in this project is scored against a reference that is itself a product — C-CAP, or an NDVI+CHM rule — and the two of them disagree over a large minority of pixels, replicated across four years and three sensors, so it is not vintage drift. Inside that contested zone no proxy can adjudicate: the corrected-label experiment lifted recall by adopting the NDVI reference's canopy DEFINITION, and whether that made the model more CORRECT or merely more LIBERAL is exactly the question a proxy cannot answer. A stratified, photo-interpreted human sample with Olofsson error-adjusted estimators is the only instrument in the pipeline with no model and no proxy product between the analyst and the answer. What would change our mind: a power analysis showing the drawn design cannot separate the two candidate canopy definitions at the n actually drawn, or strata that spend the sample on ground both references already agree about and therefore buy no adjudication at all.

The 2026-09-04 redraw's power, +-1.87pp, is recorded only in Scripts/CHATLOG.md — no design_power file exists for the redrawn kit — and it does not flip the read, because 1.87pp still sits well inside the 8.24pp separation reported at phase4/qc/design_power_2016.txt:31. That inverts the premise carried in the docstring of Scripts/qc/instruments/phase4_qc_design_power.py, which records the 2026-08-18 assessment as computing +-5.9pp under simple random sampling and concluding the sample could not arbitrate — note that design_power_2016.txt:32 records the SRS half-width the assessment assumed as +-0.0620 (6.20pp), so the two figures may be different quantities rather than one contradicting the other, and this entry does not adjudicate which. Either way sample size was never the binding constraint, interpreter fidelity is, which is why the duplicate-interpreted subset stopped being optional. The 2026-09-03 ledger audit surfaced four defects in the machinery, and the 2026-09-04 repair pass (Scripts/CHATLOG.md, `accuracy-batch-overnight`) closed them: strata rebuilt on chm2 instead of the deprecated CHM raster that reads high, the undo-as-final-row bug in `--step estimate` fixed, the 2016 and 2023n kits redrawn after 2023n was found to be a byte copy of 2022n, and the frozen-model-snapshot defect retired by U1, which scores ANY arm at the labelled points rather than the snapshot each kit froze. What remains absent is the campaign's own deliverable: no labels file exists, therefore no Olofsson estimate, no error-adjusted area, no CI. That is the honest read — the machinery is complete and gated, the number is not, and K1 (Kam labelling the redrawn 250-point 2016 kit) is the only gate between them.

entries.headline: THE ABSOLUTE FALSE-POSITIVE FLOOR IS REAL, AND LIDAR AS AN INPUT CHANNEL COLLAPSES IT.
entries.hypothesis: Every score in this pipeline is relative to an imperfect reference, so any false positive can be argued away as a reference error instead of a model error. One patch of ground in the archive admits no such argument: 2 m cells whose maximum height above ground was under 2 m in BOTH the 2005 PSLC and the 2016 USGS point clouds, eroded inward so edges cannot leak in. No model, no human and no C-CAP enters that truth definition, and a decade separates the two acquisitions that agree on it, so anything any product calls canopy there is wrong absolutely. Scoring C-CAP itself on it bounds the reference's over-call; scoring the Tier-1 arms on it asks whether the lidar-input effect confirmed against a proxy reference survives against ground that contains no proxy at all. What would change our mind: erosion too shallow to exclude crown overhang, or a flat set so small or so unrepresentative — all pavement, no yards — that its rate says nothing about the city.
entries.metric: phase4/qc/certified_flat_scores.csv — one row per scored product (both C-CAP hi-res vintages, every Tier-1 arm prob at its policy-C deployed threshold, and named citywide probs at their live thresholds): valid flat-cell count, false-positive cells, FP rate, and a note recording the operating point. Companion phase4/qc/certified_change_cells.csv carries the same pass's model-free dual-epoch loss and gain cell counts on dual-covered ground.
entries.name: certified_flat_scoring
entries.sample: the dual-lidar certified-flat cell set — 2 m cells under 2 m above ground in both the 2005 and 2016 point clouds, eroded 6 m inward — intersected with each product's valid extent. NO product sees the whole set: the full flat set is the cell count stated in phase4/qc/chm2005_validation.md, and every row of phase4/qc/certified_flat_scores.csv carries its own smaller count. Coverage varies by product rather than by footprint class, and the citywide-versus-AOI contrast inverts for at least one pair — the 2016 fullext citywide prob sees FEWER flat cells than the AOI-restricted 2006s arms — so a row's cell count is read from the file and never inferred from its footprint label. The unit of analysis is the product, one row each; the unit of evidence is the flat cell.
entries.verdict: THE ABSOLUTE FALSE-POSITIVE FLOOR IS REAL, AND LIDAR AS AN INPUT CHANNEL COLLAPSES IT. Read from phase4/qc/certified_flat_scores.csv: on physically empty ground the 2020 Tier-1 base arm calls canopy at a rate of 0.25574 while its lidar-input sibling in16 calls it at 0.0365 — an order of magnitude, measured against truth that contains no lidar-derived label and no reference product at all. That matters more than the proxy-scored version of the same claim, because it cannot be explained as the reference agreeing with the input. Three further reads live in the same file and reach the reader through the generated index rather than being restated here: the two C-CAP rows bound the reference's own over-call on flat ground, and it is small enough that C-CAP FP cannot account for arm-level FP — the arms own theirs; the 2006s label-adder arm that Tier-1 flagged as epoch poison carries the worst FP rate of any arm scored, so the poison is visible on absolute truth and not only in the ranking; and the two citywide rows show the deployed masks sit far below the AOI-restricted Tier-1 arms. The second output, phase4/qc/certified_change_cells.csv, is the model-free dual-epoch loss and gain count that the lidar decimation-null leg was judged against.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the instrument docstring, which states the design as a null before any number exists. Decimate the 2016 cloud to the MEASURED 2005 density (chunk-level Bernoulli at the coverage audit's keep probability, seeded), rebuild a 2005-style CHM using the chm2005 grid parameters, constants and class rules imported from build_chm2_2016 itself, then run the SAME LOSS/GAIN predicates certified_change_cells uses, against the real full-density product, on identical ground. True change is zero by construction, so every cell that fires is pure density artifact. The read: an artifact approaching the signal kills the leg; an artifact that is ASYMMETRIC leaves whichever direction it cannot fake still admissible, with the direction it can fake carrying the artifact as its bound.

entries.headline: DENSITY CAN FAKE GAIN AND CANNOT FAKE LOSS — that asymmetry is what revived the lidar leg.
entries.hypothesis: The 2005 PSLC cloud is about an order of magnitude sparser than 2016. Sparse sampling under-reads crown maxima, so a 2005-vs-2016 height difference can manufacture apparent canopy GAIN on ground that never changed — and if it does so at the scale of the measured signal, the whole lidar leg of the direction story is unreadable rather than positive. What would change our mind: an artifact volume comparable to the change signal in certified_change_cells.csv, in the same direction as the signal.
entries.metric: phase4/qc/lidar_decimation_null.csv — cells and km2 of artifact GAIN and artifact LOSS fired on ground where true change is zero by construction, plus the realised keep fraction and the compared-cell count. Judged against the real change signal in phase4/qc/certified_change_cells.csv; the density gap itself is measured in phase4/qc/lidar_2005_coverage_audit.md.

entries.verdict: DENSITY CAN FAKE GAIN AND CANNOT FAKE LOSS — that asymmetry is what revived the lidar leg. On ground where true change is zero, the null fired 1.5008 km2 of artifact GAIN against 0.0001 km2 of artifact LOSS, read from phase4/qc/lidar_decimation_null.csv (the row notes carry the keep probability, the seed and the predicates). Mechanism: a sparse cloud misses crown tops, so the simulated "past" reads low against a dense "now" — the artifact points one way by construction and there is no mechanism for the reverse. Consequences, both load-bearing: (1) the measured 2005->2016 LOSS in phase4/qc/certified_change_cells.csv is not reachable by the density gap and stands as physical evidence; (2) the net GAIN read carries this artifact volume as its explicit bound and is never quoted without it. This is the lidar half of the two-leg story whose human-measured half is panel_a_direction; it upgrades the pre-2016 leg from unusable to bounded, not to precise.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the C2b instrument docstring, which states the reading ladder before any arm is scored. Same arms, same test blocks, same policy-C thresholds and the same reference as the native-pixel run, so the ONLY thing that changes is how tolerance is defined; dilation is round(tol / pixel_size) pixels by 8-neighbourhood chamfer approximation, and a tolerance that rounds to zero pixels is a strict read under another name and must be reported as one, never as evidence that tolerance does not matter on that grid. The ladder is then read in three parts: strict to 1 m is boundary and registration accounting, 1 m to 2 m adds the measured registration tail from coregistration.csv, and whatever survives past 2 m is genuine detection error — the only part a recipe change or a boundary-refinement method can address. A cross-year comparison is admissible only at a fixed PHYSICAL tolerance.

entries.headline: THE STRICT SCORE WAS MEASURING PIXEL SIZE, NOT DETECTION.
entries.hypothesis: A strict per-pixel score charges a model for every boundary pixel it misplaces, and the delivery grids in the Tier-1 set differ in pixel size by more than an order of magnitude — so the same physical misplacement is nearly free for a centimetre year and fatal for a multi-metre one. The error sources that actually generate boundary disagreement are METRIC, not pixel-counted: inter-year registration measured out to metres in phase4/qc/coregistration.csv, crown-edge gradients of order a metre, and label projection from a 2020 flight onto every other year. A tolerance expressed in NATIVE PIXELS — the earlier C2 read — conflates all of that with the delivery grid and hands the coarse years metres of forgiveness while handing the fine years centimetres. What would change our mind: scores that barely move as physical tolerance grows, which would mean the disagreement is body-level rather than boundary and the strict number could stand as it is.
entries.metric: phase4/qc/metric_tolerance_scores.csv — one row per Tier-1 arm and tolerance (strict, 0.5 m, 1 m, 2 m), carrying the arm's pixel size in metres, the pixel dilation that tolerance rounds to on that grid, and recall and precision at that tolerance. The superseded native-pixel read is phase4/qc/buffer_tolerant_scores.csv from Scripts/qc/instruments/tier1_buffer_tolerant.py, retained as the artefact being corrected rather than as a source to quote.

entries.sample: nine Tier-1 arms — the base and lidar-input siblings of 2006s, 2011s, 2016 and 2020, plus 2019n base — scored on the science sample's TEST blocks against C-CAP 2021 hi-res under the forest_wetland canopy definition, each arm cut at its policy-C threshold and read at four tolerances. Not a fresh sample: the same masks the Tier-1 verdicts were written from, re-scored under a different accounting.
entries.verdict: THE STRICT SCORE WAS MEASURING PIXEL SIZE, NOT DETECTION. Read from phase4/qc/metric_tolerance_scores.csv: the 2020 base arm scores recall 0.7039 strict and 0.9197 at 2 m tolerance — the same mask, the same blocks, the same threshold, moved only by forgiving 2 m of boundary. The two 2020 arms hold the lowest strict recalls in the file and the 2020 base arm holds the highest at 2 m: the ranking inverts under nothing but a change of accounting. The file's dilate_px column carries the mechanism: on 2020's centimetre grid, 2 m of physical forgiveness is tens of pixels of dilation, while on 2006s — the only multi-metre grid in the file — both the 0.5 m and the 1 m tolerance round to no dilation at all, so its strict, half-metre and one-metre rows are identical by construction. At the one-metre-grid years, 2011s and 2016, only the half-metre tolerance rounds to zero; 1 m dilates a single pixel and does move both recall and precision. The consequence is a reader rule, not a model change: strict per-pixel recall is not comparable across delivery grids and never was a like-for-like ranking, so any cross-year arm comparison must be read at a fixed metric tolerance. This entry owns both legs of that correction — the native-pixel C2 read in buffer_tolerant_scores.csv has no registry entry of its own and is superseded here, not elsewhere. The residual past 2 m is what a boundary-refinement method would have to beat, and is the pre-written kill criterion the queued SAM pilot is gated on (WORKPLAN QUEUED).

entries.verdict: DIRECTION IS DOWN, and it is the project's only human-measured trend statement. Net 2016->2024 = -2.21pp of city area, 95% CI [-3.31, -1.11] — the single figure the city statement rests on, read from phase4/qc/panel_a_estimate.txt, which also carries every control in the same file. STANDING: Panel A is the PACE AND DIRECTION AUTHORITY. Map series corroborate it and never override it — that hierarchy is what trend8_uniform_rgb's retraction enforced, and what overlap_floor's EagleView sign test independently agreed with.

entries.headline: THE FLOOR EXISTS AND IT IS LARGE ENOUGH TO MATTER.
entries.hypothesis: Every accuracy number in this project is scored against a reference that is itself imperfect, so no reference can tell us how much of a year-to-year map difference is processing rather than trees. One pair in the archive can: 2019s and 2019n are ONE Hexagon flight delivered two ways (WA consortium 1 ft, USDA NAIP 60 cm). Identical sun, atmosphere, phenology and sensor hardware; only the delivered GSD and the processing chain differ. Whatever those two masks disagree about is a floor — no accuracy or trend claim about either product can honestly be tighter than it.

entries.verdict: THE FLOOR EXISTS AND IT IS LARGE ENOUGH TO MATTER. One flight, two deliveries, zero engine diff: canopy IoU 0.7376 and a 1.3pp citywide canopy-area gap, read from phase4/qc/sameflight_consistency.csv (the row's own note records the conditions). Two consequences, both load-bearing downstream: (1) single-year map steps inside +-1.3pp are processing, not trees — this is the error floor trend8_uniform_rgb's decision rule carries and the reason its interior wobble was declared unreadable; (2) it is the bound overlap_floor's same-window cross-delivery test was judged against, where the 2017 CoE-vs-King pair came in at one-ninth of it, confirming the noise model rather than breaking it. The IoU is the blunter of the two readings: a 0.74 IoU between two products of the SAME photons is the cleanest statement in the repo of how much of a canopy map is the processing chain.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the leaf-off instrument's own HOW-TO-READ and CAVEATS blocks, which travel with every output file and were written before this correction. The instrument's rails: GRVI is a WITHIN-FAMILY comparator, never an absolute threshold, because colour balance differs by sensor — so a comparison is legal only against a known leaf-on acquisition of the same family; the canopy mask defining which pixels are measured is a MODEL OUTPUT carrying the very blind spot under test, so the test understates low-greenness and is biased AGAINST finding leaf-off; leaf-off flights have low sun angle, so shadow and phenology are correlated and thin shadow is not excluded; the windows are a grid, not a probability sample, and the result is indicative rather than an estimate. The decisive test for the MECHANISM, stated before the histograms were run: bimodality. A distribution with a bare-deciduous mode and an intact conifer mode is phenology; a distribution shifted whole is the delivery's radiometric processing chain. Recall figures are read at each year's OWN selected threshold and are never pooled across operating-point policies.

entries.headline: THE GRADIENT IS DELIVERY RADIOMETRY, NOT PHENOLOGY, AND THE LEAF-OFF IGNORE EXPERIMENT IS DEAD AS PREMISED.
entries.hypothesis: The 2026-09-03 adversarial-review synthesis read a recall difference across five King-sensor years as LEAF-OFF PHENOLOGY — the years whose canopy pixels score least green are the years the model recalls worst — and promoted a seasonal-IGNORE training experiment on the strength of it. That reading makes a checkable commitment: if the mechanism is phenology, the low-greenness fraction has to track the calendar. It does not. The flight windows in Scripts/qc/imagery_pixelsize_and_date.csv put the two lowest low-greenness years in June and in deep winter, and all three of the highest in April, and Kam's independent observation the same day was that no leaf-off variation was visible by eye. What would separate the two mechanisms: per-bin GRVI histograms over canopy. Real leaf-off must be BIMODAL — a bare-deciduous mode beside a conifer mode, because conifers do not stop being green — while a processing-chain shift moves the WHOLE distribution, conifers included.
entries.metric: Reports/GREENNESS_GRADIENT_CORRECTION_2026-09-03.md — the owning write-up, carrying the flight-window table that breaks the phenology framing and the per-bin GRVI histogram read that resolved it. The greenness side of the association is measured in phase4/qc/leafoff_{2013,2015,2019,2021,2023}_king.csv and their .txt companions; the recall side is the citywide_rgb rows of phase4/qc/score_vs_difficulty.csv.

GRVI is computed over pixels the 2020 canopy mask calls canopy, in a subset of grid windows per year: indicative, not a probability sample.
entries.verdict: THE GRADIENT IS DELIVERY RADIOMETRY, NOT PHENOLOGY, AND THE LEAF-OFF IGNORE EXPERIMENT IS DEAD AS PREMISED. Read from Reports/GREENNESS_GRADIENT_CORRECTION_2026-09-03.md, which carries both legs: the February 2015 flight is genuinely bimodal — a bare-deciduous mode beside an intact conifer mode — and its recall is UNHARMED, so leaf-off by itself does not damage recall; while the April 2019 and 2021 deliveries show a whole-distribution shift into negative GRVI, with 74% of 2019's canopy pixels reading negative, which conifers cannot biologically be. Three consequences follow. The queued quantity-preserving leaf-off IGNORE experiment is killed at the premise: an IGNORE keyed on low GRVI would mask by radiometry, not by season, and would remove conifer canopy from supervision in exactly the years that need it. Per-delivery radiometric normalization — previously judged unnecessary — enters the candidate list for the 36-run recipe as the surviving lever, testable against the 2019 arm before any recipe change. And CLAUDE.md's durable gotcha that leaf-off years carry systematic, species-correlated label error stands entirely unchanged: that claim is about projecting an April-July 2020 label onto a February acquisition, which is a different mechanism from the recall gradient corrected here. What this entry supersedes in leafoff_recall_gradient is the CAUSE, not the measurements — the recall-versus-greenness association those five files record is unaltered, and remains directional with two named exceptions rather than a dose-response.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the instrument's own HOW TO READ and CAVEATS blocks, which are identical in all five files and which do pre-register the reading. Leaf-on reads as a unimodal positive GRVI distribution with a small low fraction; leaf-off reads as BIMODAL — conifers stay green while deciduous crowns go bare — so the low-greenness fraction is the signature. It must be compared against a KNOWN LEAF-ON acquisition rather than an absolute threshold, because colour balance differs by sensor; that is why the comparison is confined to one sensor family. The instrument also pre-registers the direction of its own bias: the canopy mask is a MODEL OUTPUT carrying the very blind spot under test, so the test understates low-greenness and is biased AGAINST finding leaf-off, which makes a positive result strong. Rails that bound any verdict: leaf-off flights have low sun angle so shadow and phenology are correlated and thin shadow is not excluded, and the sample is grid windows, "indicative, not an estimate".

Two cells break it outright, both read from phase4/qc/leafoff_*_king.csv paired against phase4/qc/score_vs_difficulty.csv: 2015 is a February flight, the catalog's leaf-off end, and carries the HIGHEST recall of the five; 2021 sits mid-pack on low-greenness and carries the LOWEST recall of the five. entries.headline: THE ANCHOR CHAIN IS CERTIFIED, AND REGISTRATION IS SEPARABLE FROM THE THING IT IS USUALLY CONFUSED WITH.
entries.hypothesis: Every cross-year statement in this project assumes the acquisitions describe the same ground. Nothing had measured that. Two things follow if it is false and unmeasured: a systematic offset between two years would be read as canopy change, and the label source itself — the 2020 flight the whole archive's supervision is projected from — could be sitting off the anchor with no one able to tell. So measure every acquisition against one anchor, on one analysis grid, in one pass: the systematic part is correctable at comparison time, and the label source's own row either certifies the chain or invalidates all of it at once.

entries.verdict: THE ANCHOR CHAIN IS CERTIFIED, AND REGISTRATION IS SEPARABLE FROM THE THING IT IS USUALLY CONFUSED WITH. The decisive row is the bridge: the 2020 label source measures p95 0.014 m against the 2020s anchor, read from phase4/qc/coregistration.csv — orders of magnitude below every other p95 in the table, which is what "gated near-zero" means and which is why the labels and the anchor can be treated as the same ground. entries.verdict: THE THRESHOLD IS THE ONE LARGE KNOB, AND THE SIEVE IS NOT ON THE TABLE — the direct answer to the question that prompted the audit. Same model, same imagery, same year: canopy area comes out 1264.0 ha or 1941.9 ha depending only on where the operating cut lands, read from phase4/qc/postproc_variant_scores.csv. Against that, the sieve is operationally invisible: in the same file, morph vs morph_sieve leaves recall unchanged to 4 dp at both cuts (0.5050 at 0.643, 0.7344 at 0.45) and moves precision only in the fourth decimal (0.8662 -> 0.8663 at 0.643, 0.7717 -> 0.7718 at 0.45, with f1 going 0.6381 -> 0.6380 at 0.643 and unchanged at 0.7526 at 0.45). Deltas of order 0.0001 do not put the sieve on the table. The epistemic claim is weaker than the write-up's phrasing, and this entry states the weaker one: "identical to four decimals at both thresholds" (Reports/RECIPE_AUDIT_2026-09-01.md) holds for RECALL only — precision moves in the fourth decimal at both cuts and f1 at 0.643 — and since NO noise floor was measured for any postproc delta, the honest reading is that the sieve's effect is UNDETERMINED, not demonstrated to be zero (CLAUDE.md 3.5). Morphology is the honest exception: its deltas are bounded small and partly absorbed by the one-u8-step difference between scorer and production, and because NO floor was measured it is UNDETERMINED-but-bounded-small, never "proven neutral" (CLAUDE.md 3.5). The operational consequence is what let the campaign proceed unblocked: exactly one item gated launch — threshold policy — and it closed the same day (entry threshold_policy_c, Kam 2026-09-01). Everything else in postproc is post-GPU and re-derivable on free CPU, so the A100 spend buys probability rasters and is insulated from every finding here. Three follow-ups stay OPEN and are not verdicts: GPKG attribute-integrity fixes (INSPECTED, not fixed; zero-GPU — do not quote GPKG area_m2 until they are), kernel unit normalisation (right on principle, measured impact nil), and the anchor-labels A/B (UNMEASURED, needs GPU).

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the selector's module docstring and the pre-registration in experiments/full_archive_e3.yaml — both written before any 36-run arm existed, so this half genuinely is pre-registered. The rule: the scorer writes an exhaustive curve at every integer u8 cut from two 256-bin histograms (the exact curve, not a sampled one) on the raw probability raster; the selector takes the HIGHEST k whose F1 is within 0.005 of the peak — deliberately NOT the argmax. Comparison is done in integer 1e-4 ticks because f1 is written at 4 dp and float subtraction drops a row sitting exactly on the boundary, always toward lower k, always against the criterion's intent. thresh is FLOOR-truncated to 6 dp so that production's int(round(thresh*254)) and the scorer's pr >= thresh*254 both cut at exactly k; rounding up silently deploys k+1. A sweep that does not hold exactly {1..254} is UNSELECTABLE and writes no row. The fallback is never circular: a missing or unscorable sweep writes no registry row, exits 2, and that year deploys a fixed 0.5 with a loud flag. The 0.005 band is asserted as METRIC INDIFFERENCE, not noise, and the docstring argues why: at ~120M scored cells the sampling error on F1 sits far below 0.005, so a plateau that wide is a property of the curve. Reader rule adopted with the policy: never pool scores across threshold policy, and never read a non-default reference row as a deployment.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the correction sequence recorded in Scripts/WORKPLAN.md row 5 and the instruments run to settle it. The discriminators were fixed by what each one can rule out, not by a target value. GEOMETRY: cross- correlate the two deliveries over candidate shifts — a correlation peaking at exactly zero shift is what one flight looks like and two flights generally are not. RADIOMETRY: fit a best-fit linear map between the deliveries and read the residual against a known baseline — a pure downsample of the same pixels leaves a residual of a couple of DN, so a residual far above that rules out one product being a resample of the other and leaves the processing chain as the difference. IDENTITY: read the date_shot and notes columns of the pixelsize table, not the source column, which holds provenance URLs and not dates — reading source alone is the specific misread that produced the wrong version of this fact. MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT: rescore the pilot's gap on a common support at several scales; if the gap collapses as support coarsens it was an artifact of scoring support and resolution is UNDETERMINED, if it holds flat the gap is real.

entries.headline: ONE FLIGHT, TWO DELIVERED PRODUCTS — and the correction runs in the direction that makes the pilot's resolution result STRONGER, not weaker.
entries.hypothesis: The 2019 pilot returned the COARSER arm scoring higher than the finer one on the same date, and how much that result is worth depends entirely on how wide the confound between the two products is. If 2019s and 2019n are two programs flying two aircraft on one date, the gap is contaminated by sensor, sun angle and atmosphere and means little. If they are ONE acquisition delivered twice, everything except delivered GSD and the processing chain is held fixed and the resolution result is correspondingly stronger. Establish which, from evidence, before quoting the pilot's gap at all.

entries.verdict: ONE FLIGHT, TWO DELIVERED PRODUCTS — and the correction runs in the direction that makes the pilot's resolution result STRONGER, not weaker. The read, from Scripts/WORKPLAN.md row 5: correlation between the two deliveries peaks at EXACTLY zero shift, while the residual after a best-fit linear map is 14-27 DN, far too large for one to be a downsample of the other, which would leave 1-2 DN — the decisive pair of figures, and the file they are read from. The identity is corroborated by Scripts/qc/imagery_pixelsize_and_date.csv, whose date_shot column records the consortium 1-ft product as the same Hexagon flight as the 2019 NAIP delivery, both at evidence grade PUBLISHED. The competing explanation for the pilot gap was killed separately: the support-matched rescore in phase4/qc/support_matched_2019_pair.csv holds the gap flat across every common support tested, so it is not an artifact of scoring the finer arm against a reference it out-resolves. STANDING: this pair is the archive's only within-flight control, and it is what experiments/sameflight_floor_c3.yaml turns into a processing-chain noise floor.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the diagnostics' own headers and footers, which state their reading rules before any verdict. (1) Compare arms at a MATCHED operating point, not at a shared nominal threshold, and read the threshold-free curve first. (2) Judge every gap against the measured retrain spread, which the curve files carry as a footer on every table — and which is explicitly a LOWER bound, because the replicates share a seed. (3) The block bootstrap answers only whether a gap survives SPATIAL resampling; a gap that clears spatial sampling but sits at the retrain scale is trajectory noise wearing a confidence interval, in that file's own words. (4) In the per-crown view, absolute touch and cover rates are NOT quotable — the 2020 crown layer is itself model output and scoring it against 2009 predictions makes real planting count as model error — so only the arm-vs-arm delta on the identical crown set is interpretable, and the honest test on it is the sign test over sector-level paired deltas, never the crown-level McNemar z, whose independence assumption CLAUDE.md rule 5 denies.

entries.headline: THE DIAGNOSTICS LANDED, AND WHAT THEY MOSTLY PRODUCED WAS A FLOOR.
entries.hypothesis: Through the pre-overhaul era every arm-vs-arm claim was a single recall number read at a single threshold, and nobody could say whether a gap between two arms was the recipe, the operating point, or the seed. 2009 became the bench where that was fixed: one year, several arms, and a family of diagnostics that each remove one of those explanations — threshold-free curves so the operating point cannot carry the answer, a paired block bootstrap so spatial sampling cannot, seed replicates so the training run cannot, a per-crown view so a pixel win that is really a boundary effect shows up as one, and a region split so over- and under-prediction are not averaged into a single score. What would change our mind about any arm ordering here: a gap that does not survive all four.
entries.metric: The threshold-free tables in Reports/ARM_PR_CURVES_2009.md and its phase4/qc/ companions (AUROC, PR-AUC, and the matched-operating-point recall at a fixed precision), the paired block-bootstrap CIs on arm gaps in phase4/qc/arm_bootstrap_ci_2009.md, the per-crown touch/cover tables in Reports/CROWN_TOUCH_2009.md, and the FP/FN-by-region tables in phase4/qc/region_confusion_2009*.md. All are computed on ONE common valid footprint — the intersection of every arm's valid pixels with the scorable reference — so the arms are never compared on different ground.

entries.verdict: THE DIAGNOSTICS LANDED, AND WHAT THEY MOSTLY PRODUCED WAS A FLOOR. The single most-cited number the pre-overhaul era owns comes out of this cluster: a recall sd of .0100 and a precision sd of .0052 across five same-seed replicates, read from the footer of phase4/qc/arm_pr_curves_2009_3band.md, which the file itself labels a LOWER bound because the replicates do not vary the seed. Every later pre-Tier-1 verdict that says "inside the noise" is measuring against that footer, and several downstream write-ups cite it for scale on years it was never measured on — legitimately, as an order of magnitude, never as a pooled sigma. On the arm ordering the cluster was built to judge, the 2009 fullext arm leads its 3-band contrast on both threshold-free metrics and at matched precision, and the per-crown view agrees in sign across every sector; the campaign's own caution is attached to that agreement, because with one training run per arm spatial consistency cannot separate "this recipe is worse" from "this run landed low". The lasting methodological output is the standard itself: matched operating points, a paired block bootstrap, seed replicates and a per-crown crosscheck became the minimum bar an arm claim has to clear, and the Tier-1 design inherited all four.

entries.headline: ALL FOUR COMMITMENTS LANDED, AND THE ASSIGNMENT IS OPT-IN BY DESIGN.
entries.hypothesis: Once two rebuilt height rasters exist alongside the one they replace, an arm's height channel stops being identifiable from its results — three products, three grids, three epochs, and a training pipeline that standardises whatever it is handed. Two things have to be pinned or every later A/B is uninterpretable. First, ENCODING: if the rebuilds do not carry byte-for-byte the same uint8 scheme as the old raster, an A/B against the old channel changes two variables at once and nothing can be attributed. Second, ASSIGNMENT: every height-channel run to date fed a roughly-2016 raster to imagery spanning a quarter century, which for the early half of the archive is a seven to sixteen year mismatch — the pipeline was using that raster as an input for years its own credibility list already excluded.
entries.metric: Scripts/pipeline/phase4seg/config.py, the append-only chm2 and chm2005 blocks — the raster paths, the shared uint8 encoding, the per-source normalisation statistics and the routine that produced them, the per-year assignment map CHM_BY_YEAR with its default and its resolver, and the tile-cache invariance argument. The same encoding is stated independently in the two standalone-ROC reports and in the accuracy sampler's own constant; those are the cross-checks, not the home.

entries.verdict: ALL FOUR COMMITMENTS LANDED, AND THE ASSIGNMENT IS OPT-IN BY DESIGN. Both rebuilds carry the old product's encoding exactly — DN = 1 + round(clip(h, 0, 50.6) / 0.2) with 0 = nodata, so height recovers as (DN - 1) * 0.2 — read from Scripts/pipeline/phase4seg/config.py, the append-only block that IS the record for this cluster. Four reads follow. (1) The 2016 rebuild's normalisation mean sits BELOW the old raster's for a reason that is itself the defect measurement: the rebuild does not inflate open ground, so far more of it is flat, and that shifts the non-zero mean down (see old_chm_defect). (2) The 2005 rebuild's statistics are trusted on a stated ground — the same routine reproduces the 2016 rebuild's published pair exactly — which is a check on the routine and not on the raster. (3) The per-year map assigns the 2005 product to the early acquisition labels listed in this entry's imagery field and keeps the 2016 product as the default, splitting at 2013 because the two clouds were flown either side of it and 2013 is very nearly equidistant; the map resolves through a single function and is reached only when an arm asks for it. (4) The trade is written down so it is not rediscovered: the 2005 product is materially coarser than the 2016 one, and the height channel's measured value is concentrated in crowns about the size of its own cell — it buys temporal correctness and pays in resolution, and the config comment records that as EMPIRICAL AND UNTESTED. That comment is now stale in one direction and deliberately not updated: the trade was subsequently tested by the Tier-1 science sample, and config.py is append-only by design. Two live consequences for readers: an arm that pinned its raster with an explicit source flag did NOT use the per-year map, and several qc instruments still name the OLD raster in their own constants, so a script's height channel must be read from the script rather than assumed from this map.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the report's own Method text, which states the reading rules ahead of every number. Four commitments. (1) INTERSECTION SCORING — every arm is scored on the intersection of all arms' valid extents with the reference's, so coverage is never charged as accuracy. (2) A PAIRED spatial block bootstrap in which every replicate scores every arm on the SAME resampled blocks, so shared ground cancels and the interval is on the DIFFERENCE; the effective sample size is the block count, not the pixel count. (3) A gap smaller than the half-width of its own paired interval is reported UNDETERMINED — "not a null: this evaluation could not tell the two apart, which is a statement about the evidence, not about the rasters." (4) EPOCH HANDICAP — an arm whose epoch differs from the reference's has real growth and removal charged to it as classification error, so its score is a LOWER BOUND on its discrimination in its own epoch. The maxN(...) arms exist to test one hypothesis: if a SHARP raster catches up once dilated to the same spatial support, the gap was granularity, not information.

entries.headline: THE SCREEN INVERTED.
entries.hypothesis: Before spending A100 hours on a height-channel training A/B, ask the cheap version of the question: does each height raster, used ALONE with no model and no GPU, separate canopy from non-canopy? Every height product in the archive is already a 254-level canopy score under one shared uint8 encoding, so sweeping the cut over every DN enumerates every "canopy iff height >= h" classifier there is. The screen was designed to fire in one direction: if a corrected raster is not a better discriminator on its own, no training arm was expected to find value in it. This run scores the three real rasters (chm, chm2, chm2005) plus dilation and two-raster-fusion arms in one sitting.

The unit of analysis is the BLOCK, not the pixel — neighbouring pixels are the same tree.
entries.verdict: THE SCREEN INVERTED. The raster independently measured to be inflated by four to five metres is the BEST standalone discriminator of the six arms — chm AUROC 0.9019 against the corrected 2016 rebuild chm2 at 0.8385, read from phase4/qc/chm_standalone_roc_all_three.md, where the paired gap and its interval sit in the same file. Three reads follow and none of them is "the old raster is good". First, the result INDICTS THE METRIC AND THE REFERENCE, not the raster: the mechanism is worked out in chm_standalone_prior_closure and the support leg in chm_roc_support_confound. Second, dilating the sharp raster toward the old one's spatial support recovers most of the difference, which is what turned "chm2 is worse" into a question about form. Third, chm2005 clears the encoding check and behaves like a correctly built product, and its score is epoch-handicapped by eleven years against a 2016 reference, so it is a floor rather than an estimate. The file bounds its own licence explicitly: this measures MARGINAL discrimination, not CONDITIONAL value — the height raster enters training as a 4th channel beside RGB, and a weaker marginal discriminator can still carry information RGB lacks. Numbers from this run are RUN-TAGGED: the synthesis report phase4/qc/CHM_STANDALONE_PRIOR_2026-08-29.md sets the rule for the whole family — "Compare numbers only *within* a run" — because each run scores on the intersection of ITS OWN arms and the footprints differ.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the report's Method text, which is the all_three run's design applied to a single hypothesis. Same shared DN sweep, same intersection scoring so coverage is never charged as accuracy, same PAIRED spatial block bootstrap with every replicate scoring every arm on the SAME resampled blocks. The reading rule is the ladder: chm2 dilated at 3 m and at 5 m, plus chm dilated at 3 m. Support is confirmed as the driver if the chm-vs-chm2 gap SHRINKS monotonically as chm2's support is matched to the old product's; it is confirmed as a property of the REFERENCE rather than of either product if blurring the old raster against itself is also rewarded. A pair whose gap is inside the half-width of its own paired interval is UNDETERMINED, never "no difference". Numbers are run-tagged and are not to be quoted against the all_three run's, because each run scores on the intersection of its own arms.

entries.headline: SUPPORT IS MOST OF IT, AND THE REFERENCE REWARDS BLUR REGARDLESS OF WHICH PRODUCT IS BLURRED.
entries.hypothesis: The standalone ROC handed back a result that reads backwards: the height raster measured to be inflated by four to five metres outscores the corrected rebuild. One explanation does not require the old product to hold more information — the reference is a generalized 1 m classified map that labels forest patches wall to wall, gaps included, while the old product's effective support is several metres and it reports a neighbourhood maximum. If that is the whole story, then dilating the SHARP raster to matched support should close most of the gap, and dilating the OLD raster against ITSELF should also be rewarded — because the reference would be rewarding blur rather than any particular product. This run tests exactly that ladder, on the chm/chm2 pair only, which buys a larger common footprint and more blocks than the all_three run.
entries.metric: phase4/qc/chm_standalone_roc_support_confound.md — per-arm AUROC / PR-AUC / best-F1 height for the dilation ladder, and the paired-gap verdict table with each pair's own resolving power. Machine copies in phase4/qc/chm_standalone_roc_support_confound_arms.csv and phase4/qc/chm_standalone_roc_support_confound_pairs.csv.
