entries.sample: the common valid footprint of the chm / chm2 dilation ladder intersected with the reference, on a 1 m analysis grid in EPSG:26910; resampled as non-empty 512 x 512 px (512 m) spatial blocks, 400 paired bootstrap replicates. The unit of analysis is the BLOCK. This run's footprint is LARGER than the all_three run's because fewer rasters intersect — the reason cross-run comparison is forbidden.
entries.verdict: SUPPORT IS MOST OF IT, AND THE REFERENCE REWARDS BLUR REGARDLESS OF WHICH PRODUCT IS BLURRED. The chm-vs-chm2 paired gap of +0.0630 dAUROC collapses to +0.0110 once chm2 is dilated to a 5 m neighbourhood maximum, read from phase4/qc/chm_standalone_roc_support_confound.md, where the intermediate 3 m rung and every interval sit in the same table. The second leg is the one that generalises: dilating the OLD raster against itself raises its best-F1 while slightly lowering its AUROC, so an operating-point statistic and a threshold-free one disagree in direction on the same treatment — quote which one you mean. What this run does NOT establish is the mechanism's completeness: a max filter cannot separate "the reference is blobbier" from "the reference is offset", which is why the registration and dilate-plus-blur runs were built; the closure is chm_standalone_prior_closure. The standing caveat is carried verbatim here as in the sibling run: this measures MARGINAL discrimination and not CONDITIONAL value, so a gap this test resolves does not license a claim about what training can do with the channel.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the report's own framing, which states the screen's purpose before any result: "if a corrected raster is not a better discriminator on its own, no training arm will find it." The reconciliation rule is the form reconstruction — apply the old product's dilate-then-blur to the sharp raster; if the entire standalone gap closes, the gap was form, not information, and the screen's premise is void. That reading is admissible only with three confounds excluded, each its own run: grid resolution (score at the sharp raster's own native cell instead of 1 m), registration (translate the sampling window, and cross-correlate the two rasters directly with no reference in the loop), and block size (512 m against 1024 m blocks — the interval must widen without any verdict changing). The interval itself is bounded by what it covers: "uncertainty from where we looked, under one reference. It is not retrain noise and not reference error."

entries.headline: FORM EXPLAINS THE GAP, THE SCREEN DID NOT FIRE, AND THE TRAINING QUESTION STAYS UNDETERMINED.
entries.hypothesis: The standalone ROC family returned a result nobody can deploy as written: the height raster measured to be inflated by four to five metres beats the corrected rebuild. Either the corrected raster genuinely holds less canopy information, or the evaluation rewards the old product's FORM — its spatial support and its smoothness, matched to a generalized 1 m reference that labels forest patches wall to wall. The two are separable with no GPU: take the old product's own two-step form (dilate, then blur), apply it to the sharp raster, and see whether the entire gap closes. If it does, the ROC was measuring form, the cheap screen's stated purpose did not fire, and the training question is still open rather than answered in the negative.

entries.verdict: FORM EXPLAINS THE GAP, THE SCREEN DID NOT FIRE, AND THE TRAINING QUESTION STAYS UNDETERMINED. Applying the old product's own dilate-then-blur to the sharp rebuild reaches AUROC 0.9073 against the old raster's 0.9059, read from phase4/qc/CHM_STANDALONE_PRIOR_2026-08-29.md — which flags the SIGN of that difference as post-hoc in the same paragraph, because it is the best of four form variants tried. The supported claim is therefore "form explains the gap", NOT "chm2 is better than chm"; quoting it the second way is the misquote the report exists to stop. Three consequences are load-bearing. (1) The metric is indicted: a constant height inflation cannot move AUROC by construction, since rank statistics are invariant under a monotone shift — level is not the treatment, shape is, and a scalar gain is something a first convolution absorbs for free. (2) All three confounds are excluded — scoring at the sharp raster's native cell barely moves the gap, the real sub-2 m registration offset is an order of magnitude too small to rank the rasters, and doubling the block size widens every interval without changing a verdict. (3) Two-raster height fusion buys discrimination nothing — the AUROC gain and the PR-AUC loss are a wash, and the PR-AUC loss is exactly what a cross-epoch maximum should cost; this is a HEIGHT fusion and must never be presented as the 5-band RGB+NIR+CHM closure. One confound is recorded as OPEN and not excluded: nothing in this repo states whether the reference product's own production chain used 3DEP-derived height, which would make the old raster partly circular with it. The screen's purpose therefore does not fire — there is no information deficit in the rebuild — so the training-side question was left open here and answered later by a different design with a different statistic, reference year and noise floor. The standing conclusion the file draws is the sharper one: THE REFERENCE IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT THE LIDAR.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the adjudication routine's own docstring, which states its admissibility conditions before reporting anything. The comparison is max return minus lowest ground-class return IN THE SAME cell, measured directly from the point pass — no ground fill, no resampling, no CRS change — so it cannot inherit a defect from either product's construction. Two confounds must be excluded before a disagreement counts as a product defect rather than an artifact: MISREGISTRATION, excluded by showing the error is minimised at zero shift (the rasters agree on where things are, not on how much), and CLASS ARTIFACT, excluded by showing the offset holds in every height bin rather than only where roofs live. The independent confirmation runs on ground certified under 2 m in BOTH lidar epochs and then eroded 6 m, specifically so no cell can excuse a tall reading as a clipped crown edge; on that ground every product should read about zero. A rebuild is only credited if it beats the old raster on that same ground.

entries.headline: THE SIGN WAS BACKWARDS AND THE DEFECT IS LARGE.
entries.hypothesis: The height channel is the largest single lever this project has measured, and the raster feeding it is a convenience product: USGS 3DEP height-above-ground at roughly 2 m, bilinear-upsampled onto a 1 m Mercator grid and quantised to uint8. The standing belief, reasoned from that upsampling, was that it reads systematically LOW — bilinear smoothing kills local maxima and a canopy apex IS a local maximum, so the loss would fall hardest on narrow conical crowns, exactly the conifer sites the project trains on. That is a chain of reasoning, not a measurement. The way to settle it is to adjudicate the raster against the raw returns with NO interpolation anywhere in the loop, and to ask not only how large the error is but which SIGN it has.
entries.metric: phase4/qc/chm2005_validation.md — the certified-flat-ground table: mean, p50/p90/p99, the share of flat ground each product asserts is taller than 2 m, and coverage, for the old raster and both rebuilds. The interpolation-free point adjudication and the coverage-confound exclusion are recorded in the append-only comment block of Scripts/pipeline/phase4seg/config.py; the corrected narrative and its struck predecessor are Scripts/IMAGERY_FACTS.md section 8.3.
entries.name: old_chm_defect
entries.sample: two independent grounds. First, every 2 m ground cell in which the point pass measured both a lowest ground-class return and a maximum canopy return — the interpolation-free adjudication. Second, the certified-flat reference raster: cells whose height above ground was under 2 m in BOTH the 2005 and 2016 clouds, eroded 6 m. The two tests report different numbers on purpose and are never averaged.
entries.verdict: THE SIGN WAS BACKWARDS AND THE DEFECT IS LARGE. On ground certified flat in both lidar epochs and eroded 6 m, the deployed raster asserts vegetation taller than 2 m on 8.82% of it against the 2016 rebuild's 0.01% — read from phase4/qc/chm2005_validation.md, where the full percentile table and each product's coverage of that ground sit in one row each. The interpolation-free point adjudication in Scripts/pipeline/phase4seg/config.py gives the mechanism and the magnitude: the product reads high nearly everywhere, in every height bin from bare ground through mature forest, and both confounds are excluded — the error is minimised at zero shift, so it is not misregistration, and it is present in the tall bins, so it is not a roof-classification artifact. The MECHANISM is that the product's effective support is several metres and each cell reports a NEIGHBOURHOOD MAXIMUM rather than the height at that cell: it smears canopy height onto the open ground beside trees. Coverage is excluded as the explanation for the rebuild's slightly smaller footprint — most of the deficit is cells the old raster itself calls short, its bilinear bleed across shoreline nodata edges. Three consequences stand. (1) Every 4-band result produced before the rebuild was earned with a channel telling the model that lawns next to trees are about five metres tall; whether that helped or hurt recall is genuinely open and is recorded as open. (2) A CONSTANT offset would be invisible to a rank statistic, which is why the standalone ROC could not see this at all — see chm_standalone_prior_closure. (3) The bias passes straight through to anything that thresholds the OLD raster at an absolute height: stable-label mining, lidar-background gating, and the height strata of the human accuracy sample. Bounded deliberately: the certified-flat subset is small, easy and non-random, so it bounds OPEN-GROUND behaviour only — accuracy under canopy, where no independent reference exists, is explicitly not established.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the arms' queue-file reads and the archived verdict prose. Three rules, one per variant, and each was stated before its result. HYBRID exists to separate label CORRECTNESS from label QUANTITY — keep the projected key, overwrite only proven pixels, IGNORE nowhere — so a null there means correcting the key is not the lever, whatever the sparse arms did. QUADRANTS was judged against a band fixed BEFORE its replicate landed: dAUROC at or above +.0060 replicates, at or below +.0020 does not stand, anything between is UNRESOLVED and must be reported as such rather than as a null (CLAUDE.md 3.5). entries.headline: CLOSED AS THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS, and the composite read is that the projected 2020 key is more right than it looks.
entries.hypothesis: Only 2020 has hand labels, so every old year is supervised by projecting the 2020 mask onto it. If that projected key is the binding constraint, then labels MINED for cross-era stability — crowns that read as canopy under every model of every era, plus dual-epoch lidar evidence of height — should beat it when training an old imagery year. Three variants attack the same question from different sides: replace the key with a sparse verified one, keep the key and overwrite only where verification exists, or add lidar-certified canopy on top of a one-variable baseline. What would change our mind is an arm that beats the projected key at a matched operating point by more than the recipe's own run-to-run spread.

entries.verdict: CLOSED AS THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS, and the composite read is that the projected 2020 key is more right than it looks. SPARSE is decisively refuted: replacing the key with a mined verified key costs 21-26 pp of recall at matched precision against a recall sd the source file itself calls a LOWER bound — the verdict prose and the matched- precision table are in archive/2026-08-pre-refactor:Scripts/CHATLOG.md, and the threshold-free curves that agree with it for the baseline arm are in Reports/ARM_PR_CURVES_2009.md. The mechanism is measured, not guessed: sparse labels BREAK CALIBRATION, parking a large share of valid pixels within a hundredth of 0.5 where the baseline parks far fewer (calibration table, same archived source), so the naive fixed-cut "recall win" for the sparse arm is an artifact of operating point. HYBRID is a clean null on the ranking metrics — recall 0.6253 at precision 0.8792 against the baseline's 0.6989 / 0.8472, both read from the live=1 forest_wetland rows of phase4/qc/qc_indep_report.csv — and the reason is also measured: the damage curve shows AUROC is flat across the whole injected label-error range, so label error moves the OPERATING POINT, not discrimination, and a sub-percent correction could never have paid. QUADRANTS is the one variant that is not dead. On the pre-registered ranking band it is UNRESOLVED, not null: AUROC gaps of +.0116 then +.0053 over the one-variable baseline, read from the curve table in phase4/qc/arm_pr_curves_2009_3band_noisefloor.md, against a band fixed before the replicate landed at +.0060 to replicate and +.0020 to fall (the band itself is recorded only in archive/2026-08-pre-refactor:Scripts/CHATLOG.md) — positive twice, above the refutation line twice, short of the replication line once. THE PAIRING IS A CHOICE, AND IT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT: both gaps are taken against the single rgb3_nodeb baseline, inherited from the source, which makes the second one cross-seed — the replicate arm scored against the base-seed baseline, while the same table also carries the baseline's own seed replicate, which this pairing never uses. The seed-MATCHED alternative on that table, nodec_s1234 against rgb3_nodeb_s1234, is a gap of +.0068, read from the curve table in phase4/qc/arm_pr_curves_2009_3band_noisefloor.md — above the +.0060 replication line, so under that pairing the ranking metric would read REPLICATES, not UNRESOLVED. The recorded read stays UNRESOLVED, under the pairing inherited from the source, pending a decision on which pairing the pre-registered band was meant to govern; nothing below changes either way. On canopy area, the deliverable metric, it REPLICATES in both runs by a margin several times the baseline seed pair's own spread, derived from the confusion counts in phase4/qc/campaign_area_reread_2009.md and phase4/qc/region_confusion_2009_replication.md — but it also roughly quadruples run-to-run variance on both metrics, so it buys accuracy and pays in stability. STANDING: the live successor is the Tier-1 lidar factor, which is a different year set, reference and statistic; nothing here pools with it.

entries.headline: THE CHECK PAID FOR ITSELF, AND IT CHANGED THE PREMISE OF THE SYNTHESIS WORK.

A brief commissioned from a session with no access to the data will state repo-specific premises it cannot check; the campaign is therefore two things: the hunt, and an adversarial check of every repo-specific claim the hunt returned against measured files. entries.verdict: THE CHECK PAID FOR ITSELF, AND IT CHANGED THE PREMISE OF THE SYNTHESIS WORK. Four of the brief's repo-specific claims are recorded as verified WRONG for this repo, including its implementation prompt, which targets a codebase whose files, tile counts and crown counts are not ours. The decisive one is the grayscale claim: the brief asserted the 1996-2003 holdings are ~100 cm and may be grayscale, and phase4/qc/imagery_qc_integrity_2026-08-24.csv records 1996_snoh_1m_rgb.tif as 3 bands at a true GSD of 100.0 cm — so the whole colorization and panchromatic-FCN thread does not apply to 1996. STANDING: this is a literature and applicability campaign, not a measurement of the model. Nothing here promotes anything; it supplies the premise degradation_synth_2000 was written to TEST, and that entry remains queued.

entries.headline: SAMPLED INFERENCE WORKS; PROMOTION DOES NOT FOLLOW FROM IT.
entries.hypothesis: Citywide inference costs a full A100 pass per arm, which is why almost no arm had ever been compared against another. If five west-east strips can stand in for the city, the same experimental question can be asked for roughly a tenth of the pixels, and the archive becomes something you can iterate on rather than something you run once. The campaign therefore asks two things at once: does sampled inference work as an experiment bench, and do the two full-extent fine-tunes it carries beat the arms already on record. What would change our mind on the second: an effect larger than the three confounds the design cannot control — the footprint, the operating point, and run-to-run training noise.

entries.verdict: SAMPLED INFERENCE WORKS; PROMOTION DOES NOT FOLLOW FROM IT. Eight arms ran VERIFY-clean and were scored, postprocessed and folded into the series, and the harness cut the cost of an inference pass severalfold — short of the design note's prediction, but real, and the report states both the measured cut and the prediction. That part landed. The promotion question came back UNDECIDABLE, and deliberately so: the campaign's own decisive read, from Reports/SECTOR_CAMPAIGN_REPORT_2026-08.md, is that 2016_fx trades recall for precision — recall 0.0473 lower and precision 0.0383 higher than the citywide arm — at a higher threshold and on a footprint with more reference canopy, so each of the three confounds independently exceeds the effect. Two things were delivered outright and are not undecidable: the study-clip coverage ceilings on 2016 and 2021s are gone, and the checkpoints exist to re-infer citywide whenever that is wanted. Two standing consequences came out of it. First, the champion ELIGIBILITY RULE now written into Scripts/pipeline/champion_arms.csv — only full-footprint rasters are champion-eligible, a sector-restricted arm tests a model and cannot be a year's deliverable — cites this campaign's section 7 as its source. The cross-registration grading rule is NOT in that docstring; it is stated in the code at Scripts/qc/imagery_qc_suite.py:460-472 and applied at :491-496. A same-year pair is read on its MEDIAN site offset, not its maximum, and what decides whether the pair gets a verdict at all is whether the five sites AGREE: NOISY is assigned on the spread of the offset vector across sites, because a real georeferencing offset is systematic while a wrong correlation peak is idiosyncratic. The correlation peak ratio is an admission floor on a single site measurement only (PEAK_FLOOR, :88), never the confidence test — a first pass that gated on peak height discarded the majority of the measurements, including parking and residential sites whose peaks are legitimately soft whenever two acquisitions differ in season or resolution, because peak height measures how ALIKE two images are and not whether the offset is right. The reference failure the design is built around is the S02-vs-U02 lesson: the plan predicted a duplicate and measurement said otherwise, so duplication is measured rather than assumed.

entries.hypothesis: The 2026-08-23/24 acquisition campaign roughly doubled the catalog and replaced several years outright, and nothing in the pipeline could say whether the new stock was USABLE. The existing catalog check answers a header question — does every entry resolve, open, and carry the bands and CRS it claims — and cannot answer the five that decide temporal canopy work: do two acquisitions of the same year land on the same ground; is any file radiometrically broken; is every "NIR" band actually NIR in the order the engine assumes; which same-year pairs are genuinely independent rather than the same pixels twice; and where are the holes, given that a coverage percentage hides interior gaps because a doughnut and a full disc score the same number. Every later imagery claim in this project rests on the answers.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the instrument's own docstring, which states the reading before the run: "Water is strongly NEGATIVE in NDVI, so a no-CHM zone that is genuinely water will show a negative NDVI distribution. Vegetation sits high. The gap between those two readings is the answer." Two design commitments make the answer admissible. First, the SAME NDVI cuts are applied to both zones, so the has-CHM zone is the control that says what green looks like in this imagery rather than a value asserted from elsewhere. Second, the bound is DELIBERATELY GENEROUS: every green no-CHM pixel is counted as canopy at each cut, even though lawns are green too, so the reported figure is an upper bound on the understatement and the truth is lower. The assumption is confirmed only if the no-CHM zone is overwhelmingly negative in NDVI AND the generous bound is negligible against the canopy figures it would perturb.

entries.headline: THE ASSUMPTION HOLDS AND IS NOW CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.
entries.hypothesis: Every canopy definition this project uses is "green AND tall", so it needs a height value. Where the lidar does not reach, a pixel CANNOT be canopy — it is forced to background by absence of data rather than by the definition, which makes every canopy figure derived that way a LOWER BOUND. A standing assumption said the uncovered strip is the Puget Sound western edge and the southern margin, i.e. water, and therefore that the bound is tight and nothing changes. That was plausible and never verified. If the uncovered zone instead contains green land, the city canopy number is understated and the canopy definition inherits a coverage bias. Water reads strongly negative in NDVI and vegetation reads high, so the two zones can be told apart with no model at all.
entries.metric: phase4/qc/chm_gap_2016.txt — the coverage split, the NDVI percentile profile of each zone with its negative-NDVI share, the green share of each zone at three NDVI cuts, and the worst-case bound on understated city canopy. Machine copy in phase4/qc/chm_gap_2016.csv, one row per zone.
entries.name: chm_gap_2016
entries.sample: the two zones of the imaged 2016 footprint — has-CHM and no-CHM — where "imaged" means red plus near-infrared above zero, measured on the 2016 four-band ortho decimated 1/8. The unit of analysis is the zone; the per-zone pixel counts and NDVI percentiles are the measurements.
entries.verdict: THE ASSUMPTION HOLDS AND IS NOW CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The worst-case understatement of city canopy from the coverage gap is up to +0.02 pp of imaged area, identical at all three NDVI cuts — read from phase4/qc/chm_gap_2016.txt, which carries the coverage split and both zones' NDVI profiles in the same file. THAT BOUND WAS MEASURED ON A CLIPPED FOOTPRINT AND MUST BE QUOTED THAT WAY: the ortho this instrument opened is the file Scripts/pipeline/phase4seg/config.py records as "2016_snoh_rgbi.tif (0.5 ft served upsample, 53.4% clip)", replaced 2026-08-23 by the native 1 ft delivery whose catalog coverage string in that same file reads "100% of city polygon, 82.3% of study extent (measured 2026-08-23; remainder is Puget Sound)". The imaged-pixel denominator and the has-CHM / no-CHM split the bound is computed over therefore describe the clipped predecessor, not the footprint the catalog now resolves to, and nothing has re-measured the bound on the replacement. The mechanism is unambiguous: almost the whole no-CHM zone reads negative in NDVI while the has-CHM zone reads like a mixed urban-forest scene, so the uncovered strip is water, exactly as the standing assumption said. Three bounds travel with this result and none of them is optional. (1) It bounds COVERAGE bias ONLY — it says nothing about whether the height raster is accurate where it does exist, and that separate question is answered badly for the raster this instrument reads: see old_chm_defect. (2) NDVI here is computed on decimated, averaged reflectance, so mixed pixels are smoothed and the percentiles are indicative rather than exact. (3) Turbid or sun-glinted water can read slightly positive, so the negative-NDVI share understates water a little — which pushes in the conservative direction for this conclusion. One unreconciled figure is recorded rather than smoothed over: the human accuracy sampler's stratum design cites a materially lower CHM coverage of the city than this file measures over imaged 2016 pixels. The two use different denominators, no tracked file reconciles them, and they must not be averaged or quoted as a contradiction.

entries.decision_rule: RECONSTRUCTED (retrospective: true) from the governing decision document and the board's standing instruction; it is a READING rule, not a pass/fail. C-CAP is a bounded comparator, never truth, and no C-CAP-referenced score may be read as evidence about our accuracy in EITHER direction. A signed net bias — and any correction factor derived from one — becomes quotable only when both limbs have been measured, because they act on the same population with opposite signs: over-call charges our true negatives as false negatives while flattering our precision, and the stands-not-crowns exclusion charges correctly detected isolated trees as false positives, understating precision on exactly the population the first limb flatters. Corollary the document states in its own right: the disagreement is a difference of KIND, not of degree, so no choice of greenness and height cutoffs can reconcile the two references — a threshold search for reconciliation is chasing something that does not exist.

entries.decision_rule: PRE-REGISTERED, before any arm has run. All constants are read from the design, not chosen after the fact. Every kill a metrics table can carry — H1-K1, H1-K2, H2-K1 INCLUDING its two-reference clause, H2-K3 and H2-K4 — is computed by qc/instruments/harm_spread.py, and H2-K2, which needs rasters, by qc/instruments/harm_change_laundering.py. Nothing is left for a reader to assemble by hand once the numbers exist. NOISE FLOOR = 0.0069 recall — the wb18 three-seed 2011s spread stated in the experiments/backbone_sweep.yaml verdict. Any per-arm delta inside it is UNDETERMINED, never "no difference" (CLAUDE.md 3.5). A SPREAD is a max-min of five draws and is noisier than one delta, so a spread change must exceed 2x floor = 0.014 to count. EXP-H1. H1-K1 (kills the workstream, and can fire): if the five-year base spread on resnet18 is <= 0.014, there is no cross-survey detection disagreement to harmonize at this sample and this encoder, and EXP-H2's premise is dead. This is not a formality: the resnet101 prior is large but the three-year resnet18 spread is small, and resnet18 gained most on exactly the two years that were worst (arm_metrics.csv / backbone_benchmark.csv). The flag fires only on a COMPLETE five-year set; a short set reads INCOMPLETE, never a pass. H1-K2 (kills the metric, not the workstream): if the 2016-referenced spread is <= 0.4x the 2021-referenced spread on the common years — i.e. >= 60% of the spread is reference epoch — then matched_p75 recall vs C-CAP 2021 is not a convergence metric and EXP-H2 must be read on the same-flight gap alone. The 0.4 is arbitrary but fixed here before any number exists, precisely so it cannot be chosen afterwards. Otherwise the spread is the pre-registered baseline EXP-H2 is read against. EXP-H2 — PROMOTE only if (P) holds AND H2-K1, H2-K2 and H2-K3 all pass. (P) CONVERGENCE: the five-year spread shrinks by >= 0.014 (2x floor). H2-K1 EPOCH LEAK, AS AN INTERACTION (this criterion has power; the record predicts it fires). "in16 > in05 on 2006s" alone is broken as a test, because chm2005 and chm2 differ in lidar density and product as well as in epoch (experiments/old_chm_defect.yaml verdict), so a uniform in16 advantage on every year is a CHM-QUALITY effect and not a leak. The leak signature is the interaction — the 2016 CHM should help a 2006 image MORE than it helps a 2016 image only if it is carrying 2016 canopy: K1 = [(in16 - in05) @ 2006s] - [(in16 - in05) @ 2016] > floor -> LEAK. Both 2016 terms are already on disk (wb18_2016_in05, wb18_2016_base) or are arm wb18_2016_in16, so the interaction costs no extra GPU. A leak verdict DISQUALIFIES in16 for time series regardless of (P). Scored against BOTH references: an interaction that appears only against C-CAP 2021 and vanishes against C-CAP 2016 is reference-epoch confounding and is reported UNDETERMINED, not as a pass. H2-K2 CHANGE LAUNDERING (direct, non-circular): over the sample-TEST blocks only, canopy-call rate of the in16 arm minus the base arm on certified 2005->2016 GAIN cells, against the same difference over all sample-test cells. If the gain-cell rise exceeds the all-cell rise beyond the floor, the channel is painting 2016 trees onto older imagery -> KILL, whatever (P) says. Certified-FLAT cells are reported in the same pass as an absolute false-positive control, separating "adds canopy everywhere" from "adds canopy where 2016 grew trees". The precedent is on the ADDER path, not the input band (experiments/tier1_science_sample.yaml verdict, add16), which is why the input band must be checked and not assumed clean. Instrument: qc/instruments/harm_change_laundering.py, written BEFORE the arms land so the kill can fire; UNVALIDATED on real rasters until it has run on them. H2-K3 MECHANISM: if the same-flight 2019s/2019n gap does not shrink beyond the floor, the treatment is NOT harmonizing delivery differences; a cross-year spread that compresses while the same-flight gap holds is evidence the compression came from reference-epoch effects -> report the cross-year result as UNINTERPRETABLE for this goal. H2-K3 reads the CHANGE in the gap, as the design writes it (in16 versus base); the ABSOLUTE gap is reported beside it and is readable, because --force-citywide gives both 2019 acquisitions ONE training recipe across their two tiers (extra.tier_flag_is_inert) — what is left between them is delivery, sensor and sampling support. VERIFY BEFORE READING IT, and it is a check on the run rather than a finding: both 2019 arms must print the same tile-index split mode at tiling. _block_partition falls back to a random split when a year has too few blocks, and a fallback on one year only would be a real recipe divergence — read it from the tile step log (CLAUDE.md 3.11), never assume it. If the 2019s arms are dropped for time, H2-K3 is UNMEASURED and the mechanism claim is UNDETERMINED for the night — it is not permitted to promote on (P) alone. H2-K4 PRE-REGISTERED NON-EVENT (so it is not read after the fact): the 2016 in16-base delta is EXPECTED to land inside the floor — resnet18 and resnet50 both read the in05 version of that delta inside their floors, and the backbone_sweep verdict attributes the resnet101's large value to a suspect-low t1_2016_base. A null on 2016 is neither a win nor a failure. SECOND QUEUE SHAPE, as the record requires: steps [labels, tile, train, evaluate] first (labels+tile on FREE CPU runtimes, the proven split, commit 7ef2f11), then a second queue with steps [inference] carrying --infer-aoi science_sample_blocks.gpkg and NO --sample-manifest (the Tier-1 ac0e79e shape), then the scoring pass (qc/instruments/score_wb50_loso.py --arms ... --refs ..., then harvest_arm_metrics). 2020 runs LAST and unbounded — the Tier-1 conveyor died at 1200 s on the 2020 arm. QUEUE-SPLIT RULE, operational and not stylistic: ALL ARMS OF ONE YEAR GO ON ONE RUNTIME. Two A100 runtimes rewrite the shared phase4/eval/semantic_eval_report.csv on every evaluate behind an async write cache, and on 2026-09-09 one arm's rows landed in neither the live report nor the archive (backbone_sweep.yaml extra.cross_vm_eval_report_clobber). Tonight that would bite on 2006s (three arms), 2019n (two) and 2019s (two). IF IT DOES NOT FIT the GPU budget, cut whole years in this order: 2020 in16, then 2011s in16. Never cut the 2006s arms — 2006s is where the spread lives — and never cut the placebo, because an in16 promotion without H2-K1 is exactly the kind of self-validated design CLAUDE.md 3.4c exists to stop.

entries.headline: TWO PRE-REGISTERED EXPERIMENTS IN ONE ENTRY, because EXP-H2 is read against a baseline EXP-H1 measures and neither is interpretable alone.
entries.hypothesis: TWO PRE-REGISTERED EXPERIMENTS IN ONE ENTRY, because EXP-H2 is read against a baseline EXP-H1 measures and neither is interpretable alone. Both are specified in Reports/HARMONIZATION_DESIGN_2026-09-10.md; this file is the commitment, the design is the derivation, and every prior number lives in the measured files the design cites. EXP-H1 — the cross-survey spread of matched_p75 recall on the working encoder cannot currently be stated: the two acquisitions that carry the resnet101 spread (2006s and 2019n) have never been run on warm-started resnet18, and resnet18 already beat resnet101 on exactly the two years that were worst (backbone_sweep.yaml verdict). Every harmonization claim is a claim about a number that does not yet exist, so H1 measures it. EXP-H2 — per-survey detection differences are driven by per-survey APPEARANCE (delivery radiometry, design 1.3; the processing-chain floor, design 1.5). Giving every year the same survey-invariant fourth band (--hs-source chm2) gives the detector a cue that does not vary by survey, so the cross-survey spread should compress, most on the years whose appearance is furthest from the training survey. WHAT WOULD CHANGE OUR MIND, stated before running: if the channel compresses the spread by IMPORTING 2016 CANOPY rather than by supplying generic structure, it manufactures false temporal stability — the precise failure this project exists to avoid. H2-K1 (an interaction) and H2-K2 (a direct per-cell count on certified change ground) are built to catch that, and the resnet101 record predicts H2-K1 FIRES. Threshold harmonization is already done and was not enough: matching the operating point moved the mean absolute year-to-year step the wrong way (phase4/qc/sensitivity_sawtooth.csv), so what is left is per-survey detector sensitivity, and the only way to remove it is to make the detector respond to the surveys more alike.

entries.decision_rule:
PRE-REGISTERED, before any run. PRIMARY KILL: healing must launder ZERO verified losses once it operates inside the Panel A window — the terminal absence of a verified loss may never be filled. That is the one result that stops the design outright, and the current 0 of 42 was measured only OUTSIDE the window, so it is not yet evidence about the case that matters.
AMENDMENT 2026-09-08, written before any arm of this campaign has a verdict and with the original text above left intact: phase4/qc/heal_gap_spectrum.csv (qc/instruments/ heal_gap_spectrum.py) measured that the PRIMARY KILL as written cannot fire. A verified loss has a terminal absence that runs to the end of the series, so the epoch after any interior epoch inside it also reads absent and a both-sides fill can never touch it; laundered_at_risk is 0 in every gap bucket on the 8-epoch stack and every alignment shift quantises to zero cells. 0 of 42 is therefore a criterion with no power, not a bound. The operative laundering test for this campaign is the FILL-SIDE audit (qc/instruments/heal_fill_audit_sample.py, ~300 fills sampled from the healer output with a null-change control, human-read, k/300 reported with its exact upper bound), together with the impossible-triple criterion at the no-change points, which keeps its power. The 42 remain the population for the ONE-SIDED failure a REVIEW-tier rule could commit (laundered_eligible = 28 at L=5). Source: Reports/LIT_HEALING_ANALOGUES_2026-09-08.md section 0 item 4 and Reports/HEALING_TOOL_REASONING_2026-09-07.md section 14.
PROMOTE if, on the 12-epoch stack: (a) laundered = 0 and terminal-censored = 0 against the frozen gold; (b) impossible-triple removal at verified no-change points is no worse than the 99 of 124 measured on 8 epochs; (c) BLIND brackets inside 2016-2024 fall to zero, which is arithmetic and therefore a check on the run rather than a finding.
RECIPE DISCIPLINE: all four arms run the trend8 recipe. The existing of_2017, of_2020 and of_2022 masks are NOT used, despite already being on disk with matched cuts, because they come from the overlap-floor campaign and mixing training recipes across a trajectory series reintroduces exactly the confound trend8 was built to control. Matched cuts collapse DELIVERY differences to 0.15 pp; that is not evidence they collapse RECIPE differences, and no measurement in the repo says they do.
Report every recall figure with the gold's measured +/- 7.3 pp. The gold is a development set: a promote here licenses the enriched confirmatory draw, not a published number.

entries.hypothesis:
The healing operator cannot currently be scored. Panel A ruled on 2016->2024, but the HEAL tier fires only on 2011s, 2013 and 2015 — every later bracket in the trend8 stack spans >= 3 years, the distance bigleaf maple coppice crosses, and is therefore BLIND. So the operator runs entirely upstream of the interval the human gold covers, and the 42 verified losses and 1,170 verified no-change points cannot judge it (measured: Reports/HEALING_TOOL_REASONING_2026-09-07.md §10).
Adding 2017, 2020, 2022 and 2023 on the SAME trend8 recipe closes every interior bracket inside the Panel A window to under three years. Two things should follow, and both are testable. First, healing begins firing where the human truth lives, so the frozen gold can score the HEAL tier directly instead of only its censoring behaviour. Second, annual cadence makes the REVIEW tier resolvable at all: post-2016 has no lidar to veto the laundering path (a real clearing whose regrowth reads as canopy), and at three-year gaps nothing in the mask distinguishes that from a detection failure — but at one-year gaps a replacement returns SMALL AND GROWING while an artifact returns FULL-SIZE AND STATIC. That is Kam's own design note, and it needs density to work.
What would change our mind: healing that launders verified losses once it operates inside the validated window, or a size-trajectory signal that fails to separate the two return shapes even at annual cadence.

(1) The sun direction is measured, not assumed: sweep candidate directions in 15-degree steps and take the one whose adjacent down-direction ground band is DARKEST in the ortho — "if no direction clearly wins, stop."
